title: Login
story: As a user, I want to log in to my account so I can access my dashboard and continue where I left off.
ac: - Login form requires email address and password - Password field includes a show/hide toggle - Incorrect credentials show a clear error message - Successful login redirects to the correct dashboard based on account type — Team Builder goes to the Team Builder dashboard, Independent goes to the Independent dashboard - 'Forgot Password?' link available on login page - 'New to Hireable? Sign up' link available on login page - Session persists until user logs out

title: Organise a Role's Work into Projects
story: As a Team Builder, I want a full-time or part-time contract's work in projects I make, each with its own progress, so that the work list doesn't pile up over the months and I can see how each body of work is going.
ac: - Projects are available once a contract is a full-time or part-time role; a trial has none, since the trial is one plan already - No project is built in: the Team Builder makes every project (a routine list is one they can add, e.g. Day-to-day); work not in a project shows as No project - When the trial becomes a role, the trial closes as its own chapter, Trial: the work finished before the role's first day, listed under Finished; whatever it left unfinished carries on outside a project as the role's work, which the trial's signed offer no longer holds (TB-077) - The work tab opens on Open work: work outside a project and the active projects - A project picker in the work header shows Open work, All work, No project with its open count (only while there's work outside a project), each active project with its progress (e.g. 4 of 5), then what's finished - The Team Builder adds a project by name (required, under 60 characters, not a name another project on the contract has, not No project or Trial), and renames, finishes or reopens the project that's showing - A project can only be marked finished once everything in it is done; the menu says how many items are still open - A finished project leaves the open work and the board; its items are kept and show under All work or the project itself - A finished project can be archived: it moves from Finished to an Archived section of the picker, and can be unarchived (reopening it unarchives it too) - A finished project, or an empty one, can be deleted after a confirmation; its work is never deleted with it — it stays outside a project with its history, and each item's feed says the project was deleted - No project can be created, archived or deleted while the contract is a trial, in the app or through the API - Work outside a project finished more than 14 days ago leaves the open work the same way - The summary's N of M done counts the work that's showing - A task added while a project is showing, or in a project's column when grouped by project, goes into that project; elsewhere it goes outside a project - The Team Builder moves work into, out of and between the active projects from the task's Project field or by dragging it between project columns; each move is logged on the task - The Independent Contractor sees the projects and each task's place, but can't add, change or move them - Group by Project is offered on the Board, List and Timeline - Finished work is read-only: the trial's chapter once the contract is a role, and a finished or archived project's work, can't be edited, moved, re-statused or commented on, and nothing can be added while one is showing (the banner says why) - Reopening a project makes its work editable again; the trial's chapter stays as it was

title: Sign Up as Team Builder
story: As an employer, I want to create an account so I can post jobs, review talent, and manage my hiring needs.
ac: - Sign up form requires: full name, email, password, company name - Email must be unique — duplicate emails show an error - Password must meet minimum requirements (8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number) - After submitting, user receives a verification email - Work Style Quiz is presented as a required step before accessing the dashboard - Completing the quiz generates workplace tags and work style profile - After quiz completion, user is redirected to the Team Builder dashboard - Account Setup Checklist is shown on first login

title: Sign Up as Independent Contractor
story: As a remote talent, I want to register on the platform so I can find jobs, join Trial Drives, and connect with employers.
ac: - Sign up form requires: full name, email, password, job title - Email must be unique — duplicate emails show an error - Password must meet minimum requirements (8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number) - After submitting, user receives a verification email - Work Style Quiz is presented as a required step before accessing the dashboard - Quiz asks 6 questions about work style, communication, and decision-making approach - Multiple choice answers available per question plus a free-text 'Something else' option - Completing the quiz generates workplace tags/badges visible on the talent's profile - After quiz completion, user is redirected to the Independent dashboard - Account Setup Checklist shown on first login

title: Reset Account Password

ac: - 'Forgot Password' link available on login page - Entering a registered email sends a password reset link - Unregistered email shows an error - Reset link expires after 24 hours - New password must meet minimum requirements - Success message shown after password is successfully reset - User is redirected to login page after reset

title: View Dashboard
story: As an employer, I want to see a personalized dashboard when I log in, so that I can quickly get an overview of my account activity and know what to do next.
ac: \* Dashboard loads upon login showing all key widgets \* Displays personalized greeting with employer's first name (e.g.

title: Quick Access to Work to Review and My Tasks
story: As a Team Builder, I want the work waiting on my review and my own open tasks on my dashboard, so that I can review submissions and keep my side of the work moving without opening each contract first.
ac: - While a contract with a work list is live, the dashboard shows My tasks under the greeting: who and which role, and how many items are waiting on review, To do and In progress - It lists up to five, most pressing first: the Independent Contractor's work sent for review, then the Team Builder's own and unassigned tasks — overdue, in progress, then To do by due date (undated last) - A review row shows a Review call to action; the others show their due date (Overdue in red), and unassigned ones say so - Clicking a row opens that task in its panel on the contract's Work tab, where a submission has Approve and Request changes; the arrow and "N more in the Work tab" open the Work tab - The Independent Contractor's work that isn't in review, and done or deleted work, isn't listed; with nothing waiting, it says so - Without a live contract the card isn't shown

title: Send Message

ac: - Employer can compose and send a message to any talent they have an active connection with - Message is delivered in real time - Sent messages appear in the conversation thread immediately - Empty message cannot be sent

title: Receive Message
story: As an employer, I want to receive messages from talents and candidates, so that I can stay updated on their responses and keep communication in one place.
ac: - Employer receives messages from talents in real time - New messages trigger a notification - Messages appear in the correct conversation thread - Unread count updates automatically

title: Show Unread Indicator

ac: - Unread message count is displayed on the Messages nav icon - Count updates in real time when new messages arrive - Count clears when the conversation is opened

title: Search Messages

title: Attach Files in Messages

title: Start / Join Call
story: As an employer, I want to attach or share a meeting link in a conversation, so that I can easily schedule or start a call with a talent or candidate without leaving the platform.
ac: - Call button available within an active conversation - Clicking initiates or joins a call session - Notification sent to the other party when call starts

title: Browse Independents
story: As an employer, I want to browse a list of available independent talents, so that I can find candidates that fit my role and requirements.
ac: \* Discover page displays a list of available Independent Contractor profiles \* Each card shows: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, skills, and match percentage \* Results load with pagination at the bottom \* Pagination shows: Previous, page numbers, and Next \* Current page number is visually highlighted \* Empty state shown if no profiles are available \* Search bar available on Discover Independents page — searches by name, role, or skills \* Results update dynamically as Team Builder types \* Search shows a clear (X) button when active — clicking restores the full list \* Empty state shown when no results match \* Filter panel accessible from the Discover page \* Filter options: Experience Level, Skills, Salary Range \* Multiple filters can be applied simultaneously \* Apply Filters button confirms the selection \* Reset Filters button clears all active filters \* Active filters are visually indicated \* Match percentage displayed as a badge on each talent card \* Color coded: green (high), yellow (medium), grey (low) \* Phase 1 (Work Style only) shown before any job post exists \* Phase 2 (+ Job Post & Profile) shown when a job post is active \* Phase 3 (+ Trial Performance) updates during trial \* Phase 4 (+ Evaluation) final score after evaluation is submitted \* Tooltip explains what the score is based on \* Clicking a talent card opens their full profile \* Profile shows: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, website, LinkedIn, bio, workplace tags, skills, and performance history \* Match percentage prominently displayed on profile \* Invite to Propose and Save buttons available on the profile \* Read-only view

title: Invite Independent to Apply
story: As an employer, I want to invite an independent to apply for one of my jobs, so that I can proactively reach out to strong candidates who haven't applied yet.
ac: Invite to Propose button available on talent profile and discover card Modal shown to select which active job post to invite them to Talent receives a notification of the invitation Expectations from the selected job post are unlocked and visible to the talent upon invitation Confirmation shown after invite is sent The invited talent shows in the role's Matched column as Awaiting application until they apply; Invite to interview stays disabled until then, saying they haven't applied yet Inviting a talent whose application for the same role was dropped (and deleted from the tracker) reopens the role for them: they can apply again, and the new application moves through the pipeline as usual

title: Save Independent

title: View Saved Independents
story: As an employer, I want to see all the independents I've saved in one place, so that I can easily revisit and compare my shortlisted candidates.
ac: \* Saved Independents page shows all Independent Contractor profiles the Team Builder has saved \* Each card shows: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, skills, and match percentage \* Match percentage color coded: green (high), yellow (medium), grey (low) \* Score updates dynamically as phases progress \* Tooltip explains what each phase score is based on \* Results load with pagination at the bottom \* Pagination shows: Previous, page numbers, and Next \* Filter panel accessible from Saved Independents page \* Filter options: Experience Level, Skills, Salary Range \* Multiple filters can be applied simultaneously \* Apply Filters button confirms the selection \* Reset Filters clears all active filters \* Active filters are visually indicated \* Empty state shown if no Independent Contractors have been saved

title: Remove from Saved
story: As an employer, I want to remove an independent from my saved list, so that I can keep my shortlist clean and relevant.
ac: \* Remove button available on each saved Independent Contractor card \* Confirmation prompt shown before removing \* Removing takes effect immediately \* Independent Contractor is NOT notified when removed

title: Invite Saved Independent to Apply
story: As an employer, I want to invite a saved independent to apply directly from the saved list, so that I can act without navigating back to discover.
ac: \* Invite to Propose button available on saved Independent Contractor cards \* Modal shown to select which active job post to invite them to \* Independent Contractor receives a notification of the invitation \* Expectations from the selected job post are unlocked and visible to the Independent Contractor upon invitation \* Confirmation shown after invite is sent

title: Create Trial Job Post
story: As a Team Builder, I want to create a trial role so that I can evaluate a talent's real-world performance before hiring them full-time or part-time.
ac: - Create Role offers two cards: Test Independents (trial) and Build Team (full-time or part-time) — selecting Test Independents starts a trial post - The trial path has 5 steps: Role Details → Trial Tasks → Budget & Duration → Review → Publish - Role Details requires: role title, role description (up to 500 characters), 1 to 5 skills, experience level, and how many to hire - Trial Tasks is a Notion-style list of what the Independent Contractor should get done in the trial: type a task and press Enter for the next, and give each a due week (Week 1 to the trial's last week), a priority (Low / Medium / High), and details if needed — at least one task is required - Optional notes (up to 500 characters) and a link attachment, such as a Loom video or Google Doc, can go beside the tasks - The trial's tasks are only shared with Independent Contractors the Team Builder invites or matches with — the public role listing says how many there are, not what they are - Budget & Duration requires a monthly rate range (minimum and maximum, the minimum can't be more than the maximum) and a trial duration of 30, 60, or 90 days - Next stays disabled until every required field on the step is filled - A role template can fill in the role, description, skills, experience level, trial tasks, trial duration, and rate range — if the form already has values, the Team Builder confirms before they are replaced - Review shows every section with an edit option on each, so details can be changed in place before publishing - Save as draft is available at every step and keeps everything entered so far - Publishing requires a complete company profile and a payment method on file — until both are in place, Publish is blocked with a prompt to finish them, and the role can still be saved as a draft - Published role appears in All Roles with Active status and a TRIAL badge, and becomes visible to Independent Contractors - Candidates for a trial role are hired onto a paid trial: the offer sets the trial's start and end dates and funds escrow for it - The trial's tasks go into each offer as the proposal settles them (TB-105, TB-106): what each task's plan sets — its name, details, due week and priority — is what both sides sign, and stays as agreed once it's signed (TB-077)

title: Create Full-Time Job Post
story: As a Team Builder, I want to create a full-time role so that I can attract and hire the right talent for a long-term engagement.
ac: - Team Builder selects the Build Team card on Create Role and sets Employment type to Full-time on the first step - The full-time path has 5 steps: Job Details → Salary & Start → Exclusive Benefits → Review → Published - Job Details requires: role title, role description (up to 500 characters), 1 to 5 skills, experience level, and how many to hire - Salary & Start requires a monthly salary range (minimum and maximum, the minimum can't be more than the maximum) and a start timing: Immediately, In 2 weeks, or In 1 month - Exclusive Benefits is optional and can be skipped: Health Insurance Coverage, Government Contribution Coverage, Internet Allowance, and Learning & Development Allowance, each with its own monthly amount - A note explains that exclusive benefits apply to full-time hires only and are reimbursed against proof of payment (receipts) - Next stays disabled until every required field on the step is filled - A role template can fill in the role, description, skills, experience level, and salary range — if the form already has values, the Team Builder confirms before they are replaced - Review shows every section with an edit option on each, so details can be changed in place before publishing - Save as draft is available at every step and keeps everything entered so far - Publishing requires a complete company profile and a payment method on file — until both are in place, Publish is blocked with a prompt to finish them, and the role can still be saved as a draft - Published role appears in All Roles with Active status and a FULL-TIME badge, and becomes visible to Independent Contractors - A full-time role hires directly with no trial: after the proposal, the signed offer starts the full-time contract — no escrow, no end date, paid monthly

title: Create Part-Time Job Post
story: As a Team Builder, I want to create a part-time role so that I can hire talent for a set number of hours a week on an ongoing basis.
ac: - Team Builder selects the Build Team card on Create Role and sets Employment type to Part-time on the first step - The part-time path has 4 steps: Job Details → Rate & Hours → Review → Published - Job Details requires: role title, role description (up to 500 characters), 1 to 5 skills, experience level, and how many to hire - Rate & Hours requires a monthly rate range (minimum and maximum, the minimum can't be more than the maximum), hours per week (10, 20, or 30 hrs a week), and a start timing: Immediately, In 2 weeks, or In 1 month - Part-time roles have no Exclusive Benefits step — exclusive benefits are for full-time roles only - Next stays disabled until every required field on the step is filled - A role template can fill in the role, description, skills, experience level, and rate range — if the form already has values, the Team Builder confirms before they are replaced - Review shows every section, including hours per week, with an edit option on each - Save as draft is available at every step and keeps everything entered so far - Publishing requires a complete company profile and a payment method on file — until both are in place, Publish is blocked with a prompt to finish them, and the role can still be saved as a draft - Published role appears in All Roles with Active status and a PART-TIME badge, and becomes visible to Independent Contractors with its hours per week - A part-time role hires directly with no trial: after the proposal, the signed offer starts the part-time contract — no escrow, no end date, paid monthly

title: View Posted Roles
story: As an employer, I want to see all my posted jobs in one list, so that I can monitor and manage all my active, closed, and draft listings in one place.
ac: \* All Roles page lists all job posts created by the employer \* Each card shows: job title, type badge (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), status (Active / Closed / Draft), date posted, and pipeline stats (Candidates, Matched, Offer Sent, Hired, Dropped) \* Active roles show colored pipeline stat badges \* Closed roles show greyed out pipeline stat badges \* Draft roles show -- on all pipeline stats and no date posted \* Search bar available — searches by job title and updates dynamically \* Filter by Status: Active, Closed, Draft \* Filter by Type: Trial, Full-Time, Part-Time \* Both filters can be applied simultaneously \* Clearing filters restores the full list \* Three-dot menu available on each card for additional actions \* Post a Job button available at the top right and navigates to Create Role \* Empty state shown if no roles exist

title: Duplicate a Job Post
story: As an employer, I want to duplicate an existing job post, so that I can reuse the details for a similar role without filling out the form from scratch.
ac: - Duplicate button available on any job post - Creates an identical copy saved as Draft - Duplicated post appears in Posted Jobs list with Draft status - All fields are editable before publishing

title: Close Active Job Post
story: As an employer, I want to close an active job post, so that I can stop receiving new applications when I no longer need candidates for that role.
ac: - Close button available on Active job posts only - Confirmation prompt shown before closing - Closed post status changes to Closed and is no longer visible to talents - Existing applicants remain in the pipeline

title: Delete a Job Post
story: As an employer, I want to delete a closed or draft job post, so that I can keep my list clean and remove roles I no longer need.
ac: - Delete button available on Draft job posts only - Confirmation prompt shown before deleting - Deleted post is permanently removed - Active or Closed posts cannot be deleted

title: Reopen a Closed Job Post
story: As an employer, I want to reopen a closed job post, so that I can resume receiving applications if my hiring needs change.
ac: - Reopen button available on Closed job posts only - Confirmation prompt shown before reopening - Status changes back to Active - Post becomes visible to talents again

title: Edit a Draft Job Post
story: As an employer, I want to edit a draft job post, so that I can update or complete the details before publishing it.
ac: \* Edit option available in the three-dot menu on Draft job post cards only \* Clicking the Draft card or selecting Edit from the three-dot menu triggers the same behavior \* If draft was created from scratch — employer is redirected to the exact step where they left off with all previously filled fields retained \* If draft was duplicated from an existing job post — employer is redirected directly to the Review Job Post page with all fields pre-filled \* All fields are editable regardless of how the draft was created \* Save as Draft button available to save changes without publishing \* Publish option available in the three-dot menu on Draft cards — all required fields must be completed before publishing \* Clicking Publish changes the status from Draft to Active immediately \* Published role appears in All Roles with Active status and becomes visible to Independent Contractors \* If required fields are incomplete, publish is blocked and employer is prompted to complete missing fields

title: View Candidate Tracker
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view all candidates in a pipeline so that I can track where each candidate is in the hiring process.
ac: \* Applicant tracker opens showing a Kanban-style pipeline with 7 columns: Candidates, Matched, Interview, Proposal Requested, Offer Sent, Hired, Dropped \* Each column shows a total count of candidates at the top \* Each card shows: candidate photo, name, role, rate, experience level, match percentage, status badge, and timestamp \* Candidates column shows all Independent Contractors who applied to the job post \* Matched column shows candidates automatically matched by the system based on fit score \* Invite to interview is only for candidates who have applied: a match invited to apply who hasn't applied yet shows it disabled, saying they haven't applied yet, on the card and on their profile \* Match percentage is color coded: green (high), yellow (medium), grey (low) \* Message icon visible on each card — unread messages show a red notification badge \* Clicking the message icon opens the messaging interface with that candidate pre-selected \* Unread messages show a red notification badge on the message icon \* Back to jobs link available at the top to return to All Roles \* Two tabs available at the top: Candidates and Job Details \* Job Details tab shows: job title, type (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), status, role description, required skills, experience level, and budget \* Job Details tab is read-only — no editing available \* Team Builder can switch between Candidates and Job Details tabs without losing pipeline state \* When an Independent Contractor applies, the system automatically calculates their match percentage and places them in the Candidates column \* High fit score candidates are automatically moved to the Matched column \* Interview column shows status badges: Awaiting confirmation, Interview confirmed, Interview completed \* Proposal Requested column shows status badges: Awaiting proposal, Revision requested, Proposal submitted \* Offer Sent column shows status badges: Awaiting response, Offer declined \* Review Sent Offer button appears on cards in the Offer Sent column \* Clicking Review Sent Offer opens the full offer details: job role, trial duration or start date, budget, agreed tasks, and current status \* Offer details are read-only — offer cannot be edited after sending \* If offer is declined, card status updates to Offer declined and Team Builder is notified \* Hired column shows all Independent Contractors who accepted the offer \* Each hired card shows: candidate photo, name, role, match percentage, Hired status badge, and start date \* Clicking a hired card navigates to the contract dashboard (trial, full-time or part-time) for that Independent Contractor \* Hired candidates cannot be dropped from the pipeline \* Dropped column shows all dropped candidates with greyed out cards

title: Invite Candidate for Interview
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view a candidate's full profile so that I can review their background, skills, and match percentage before taking action.
ac: \* Clicking a candidate card opens their full profile \* Profile shows: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, bio, workplace tags, skills, and performance history \* Match percentage prominently displayed \* Read-only view from the pipeline \* Invite for Interview and Request Proposal buttons available depending on pipeline stage

story: As a Team Builder, I want to invite a matched candidate for an interview so that I can assess them further before requesting a proposal.
ac: \* Clicking a candidate card opens their full profile \* Profile shows: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, bio, workplace tags, skills, and performance history \* Match percentage prominently displayed \* Read-only view from the pipeline \* Invite for Interview and Request Proposal buttons available depending on pipeline stage

title: Request Proposal from Candidate
story: As a Team Builder, I want to request a proposal from a candidate so that I can review their terms and cover letter before sending an offer.
ac: \* Request Proposal button available on cards in the Matched and Interview columns \* Clicking sends a proposal request to the Independent Contractor \* Candidate moves to the Proposal Requested column \* Card status updates to Awaiting proposal \* The trial's tasks from the job post are shown to the Independent Contractor with the request, so their proposal prices them — the Independent Contractor proposes terms, not tasks \* Independent Contractor receives a notification to submit a proposal \* Confirmation shown to Team Builder after request is sent

title: View Proposal
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view a proposal submitted by a candidate so that I can review their terms and cover letter against the role's tasks before making a decision.
ac: - Review Proposal button appears on cards with Proposal submitted status in the Proposal Requested column - Clicking opens the full proposal submitted by the Independent Contractor, with the candidate's photo, name, role, and match percentage - The trial's tasks from the job post are shown beside the proposal — each with its title, due week, priority (Low / Medium / High), and description — so the proposal can be read against the work it prices; a proposal sent before tasks were the Team Builder's to set shows the tasks it listed - Proposal shows the proposed terms: rate (trial), expected salary (full-time), or monthly rate and hours per week (part-time), and the start date proposed — on a trial with the end date it comes to - Proposal shows the cover letter and, when added, a portfolio or work samples link - The role's own terms are shown alongside so the proposal can be read against what was asked for: contract type, posted budget or salary range, and trial duration or start timing — plus the trial's notes on a trial role and the hours per week the part-time role was posted at - Three actions are available from this view: Send offer, Request revision (a note is required), and Decline; Send offer waits until each suggested task change is accepted or ignored

title: Request Changes to Proposal
story: As a Team Builder, I want to request changes to a proposal so that I can negotiate the terms before committing to a trial.
ac: \* Request revision button available when viewing a submitted proposal \* Team Builder must provide feedback or specify what needs to be revised \* Independent Contractor receives a notification of the revision request \* Card status updates to Revision requested in the Proposal Requested column \* Review Proposal button remains visible for Team Builder to track resubmission \* Independent Contractor can revise and resubmit — card status updates to Proposal submitted upon resubmission - A revised proposal shows the talent's suggested task changes, each with their reason; the Team Builder accepts or ignores each one (and can change their mind until the offer is sent) - Accepted suggestions go into the offer's tasks as they stand — the offer doesn't edit them; ignored ones change nothing - A revision is how anything in the proposal changes — the rate, the hours, the start date, the tasks — since the offer carries what the proposal settled (TB-105)

title: Decline Proposal
story: As a Team Builder, I want to decline a proposal so that I can remove a candidate from consideration.
ac: \* Decline button available when viewing a submitted proposal \* Confirmation prompt shown before declining \* Independent Contractor receives a notification that their proposal was declined \* Candidate moves to the Dropped column upon decline \* Card is visually greyed out in the Dropped column

title: Send Offer
story: As a Team Builder, I want to accept a candidate's proposal and send them an offer so that I can move forward with hiring them.
ac: - Send offer button available when viewing a submitted proposal, once each of the talent's suggested task changes is accepted or ignored - A trial offer has a 5-step progress stepper: Offer Letter → Tasks → Start & End Dates → Deposit Payment → Review & Sign - A full-time or part-time offer has a 4-step progress stepper: Offer Letter → Tasks → Start & Salary (full-time) or Start & Hours (part-time) → Review & Sign — no deposit, no escrow, and no end date - Step 1 (Offer Letter) shows: candidate profile, match percentage, experience level, location, proposed rate or salary (plus hours per week on a part-time role), skills, and cover letter - The offer carries what the proposal settled (TB-106), and none of it is edited here: the tasks, the start date, and the pay and hours - Step 2 (Tasks) shows the tasks the proposal settled, read-only: the job post's, with the suggestions the Team Builder accepted, each with its due week as the date it becomes, priority and details — a trial needs at least one; a full-time or part-time offer carries none unless the proposal settled some, since the work is added once the contract starts - Trial step 3 shows the start date the Independent Contractor proposed (IN-072) and the end date it comes to from the trial duration (30, 60, or 90 days), counting working days only — weekends are excluded; a proposed start that has passed stops the offer until a revision gives a new one - Trial step 4 (Deposit Payment) charges the escrow — the monthly rate × the number of trial months — plus a 10% platform fee on top, to the payment method on file - A trial offer can't continue until the deposit is made; the escrow is held until the trial ends, and the platform fee is not refunded - Full-time step 3 shows the start date and the monthly salary the proposal settled, and sets the exclusive benefits included - Part-time step 3 shows the start date, the monthly rate, and the hours per week the proposal settled - A proposal from before a start date was asked for reads as the earliest start: today on a trial; on a full-time or part-time offer, the role's posted start (immediately, in 2 weeks, or in 1 month from today, a weekend moving to the Monday) - Review & Sign shows a summary of the offer (role, candidate, pay, dates, the number of tasks, and on a trial the escrow and platform fee), and the Team Builder signs by typing their full name - Signing sends the offer: the candidate moves to the Offer Sent column with status Awaiting response, and the Independent Contractor is notified - A sent offer isn't edited: Sent Offers can only withdraw it, and a new offer follows a revised proposal

title: Drop / Undrop Candidate
story: As a Team Builder, I want to drop or undrop a candidate from the pipeline so that I can control which candidates continue in the hiring process.
ac: \* Drop option available on any candidate card at any pipeline stage \* Drop and Undrop are confirmed in a dialog first (the same one from the card and the candidate's profile), never done on a single click; Cancel leaves the candidate as they were \* Dropped candidate moves to the Dropped column and card is visually greyed out \* Independent Contractor is NOT notified when dropped (no notification), but their own application reflects it: its status reads Not moving forward, the card is greyed out, the application page says the company isn't moving forward, and nothing on it can be acted on (no proposal, no interview reply); undropping restores it \* Undrop button available on Dropped cards to restore the candidate to their previous stage \* Candidate is NOT notified when undropped \* Delete button beside Undrop on Dropped cards removes the card from the role's tracker for good, after a confirmation, so the Dropped column doesn't pile up; only dropped cards can be deleted, the candidate is NOT notified, and their own application record and any past interview are kept

title: View All Independents
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see all my Independent Contractors in one list so that I can monitor everyone I am currently or previously working with.
ac: \* All Independents page lists all Independent Contractors with an active or past contract \* Each card shows: photo, name, role, contract type (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), task summary, and contract status \* Default view shows active contracts only \* Search bar available — searches by name or role and updates dynamically as Team Builder types \* Search shows a clear (X) button when active — clicking restores the full list \* Empty state shown when no results match with options to Adjust filters or Clear search \* Filter dropdown available with options: All, Trial, Full-Time, Part-Time \* Filter applies immediately and active filter is visually indicated \* Empty state shown if no Independent Contractors exist with options to Discover Independents or Create Job Post \* Info note shown on empty state:

title: Show / Hide Inactive Talents
story: As a Team Builder, I want to toggle inactive Independent Contractors on or off so that I can view ended contracts when needed without cluttering my active list.
ac: \* Show Inactive toggle available at the top of the All Independents page \* Default state is OFF — only active contracts are shown \* Toggling ON shows both active and inactive contracts \* Inactive cards are visually greyed out to differentiate from active ones \* Inactive cards show: ended date instead of days remaining or start date \* Toggling OFF hides inactive contracts and restores active-only view

title: Open Talent Dashboard
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see a summary card for each Independent Contractor showing their tasks, contract type, TFS score, and contract status so that I can quickly assess their performance at a glance.
ac: - Each card shows: photo, name, role, and message icon - Task summary shows four counts: Tasks (all tasks), In progress, Overdue (past their due date and not Done), and Done - In progress count is highlighted in blue, Overdue in red, and Done in green - Contract type badge shown: TRIAL (orange), FULL-TIME (blue), or PART-TIME (magenta) - Trial cards show a TFS pill with the percentage, and the days remaining - Full-time and part-time cards show the contract start date — no TFS pill - When 7 days or fewer remain on a trial, the days remaining text turns orange as a warning - When a trial has ended, the card shows an Evaluate now button, replaced by the evaluation result once the evaluation is submitted - Clicking a card opens that Independent Contractor's Trial Dashboard, or their Full-Time and Part-Time Dashboard

title: Evaluate Independent from Card
story: As a Team Builder, I want to evaluate an Independent Contractor directly from their card when their trial ends so that I can quickly submit my assessment without navigating to their full dashboard.
ac: \* Evaluate now button appears on Trial cards only when the trial end date has passed \* Clicking Evaluate now navigates to the post-trial evaluation form for that Independent Contractor \* Button is not visible during an active trial — only shown when trial has ended \* After evaluation is submitted, the Evaluate now button is replaced with the evaluation result

title: View Trial Dashboard
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view the trial dashboard of an Independent Contractor so that I can monitor their overall trial performance, activity, and fit score in one place.
ac: - Dashboard header shows: Independent Contractor name, role, and contract status badges (Trial, Active) - A contract signed ahead of its start date shows Starts <date> in place of its status until that day, and the activity tracker starts counting from then rather than showing the Independent Contractor as Unresponsive - Send Message button is visible in the header at all times - File a Dispute button is visible in the header at all times - Navigation tabs visible: Tasks, Contract & Payment, Evaluation - Tasks tab is the default view when the dashboard loads - Summary stats bar shows: Tasks count, Done count, Days left with the trial date range (e.g. Jan 01 – Feb 03, 2026), and Waiting for review count - Trial Fit Score (TFP) widget shows the overall score as a percentage, broken down into Performance, Profile, and Work Style — each with a progress bar and percentage - Performance is the share of trial tasks that are Done (Done trial tasks ÷ all trial tasks) - Tooltip explains how the score is calculated and when the final score becomes available - Phase weights update automatically based on the current phase: On Trial (Phase 3): Work Style 20%, Profile 30%, Performance 50% — Evaluation excluded; Post Trial (Phase 4): Work Style 15%, Profile 20%, Performance 40%, Evaluation 25% - Tasks tab shows the shared task list both sides work in, in List view by default; what the signed offer set of its tasks shows a lock (TB-077) - The trial's tasks are the ones agreed in the signed offer: the Independent Contractor works them, and no new tasks are added to a trial (TB-064) - When tasks are waiting for review, a banner at the top of the dashboard says how many, and its action opens one in the task details panel - Activity heatmap shows a GitHub-style Mon–Fri daily grid — weekends are not shown - Each tile shows one of three states: green — the Independent Contractor submitted a task for review that day; light green — they worked on tasks (moved one or ticked a subtask); grey — no task activity that day - The Independent Contractor's current streak is displayed: consecutive weekdays with any task activity, with its status label (Thriving / Idle / Unresponsive) - When the trial closes, the tracker shows the final streak

title: Open Task Details
story: As a Team Builder, I want to open an item in a details panel so that I can see everything about it and act on it without leaving the view I'm in.
ac: - The panel slides in over the view as a focused sheet: the page behind it waits until the sheet is closed — with Escape, the close button or a click outside — and it's full width on a phone - The item's number and name head the sheet and stay in view while the rest scrolls; the name is edited right there and wraps rather than being cut off - The panel shows and edits: name, status, assignee, work type, priority, start and due dates, effort, tags, dependencies (what it waits on and what it blocks), description, subtasks with progress, who added it and when, and who last changed it - What this person may not change reads as plain text rather than a control that would fail — or, where a task's signed offer set it, with a lock that says so (TB-077) - When the item is In review, the panel shows Approve and Request changes (which needs a note), with the Independent Contractor's note for the reviewer - One activity feed shows the item's history and comments together, oldest first - Typing in the name or description keeps a draft: if someone else changes the same text meanwhile the draft isn't wiped — the panel says so, and saving checks first (TB-144) - The panel's address (?task=…) survives a reload and is what notifications link to — a comment's notification opens it on its comments (?focus=comments); an item that no longer exists says so - Focus moves into the panel when it opens, onto its close button, so the name doesn't open for editing each time; Escape in a field only leaves that field, and the next Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the card or row it came from

title: Switch Between Work Views
story: As a Team Builder, I want to switch the work between Board, List, Calendar, Timeline and Workload so that I can see it as cards, rows, dates, a schedule or who has what.
ac: - A view switch sits at the top of the Work tab: Board (the default), List, Calendar, Timeline, Workload - It is a tab list: the arrow keys move between views and Enter or Space opens one; moving focus alone doesn't switch - Every view reads the same items — switching never copies or changes them - The view is kept in the address (?view=…): a reload or a shared link opens the same view, and Back and Forward move between the views visited - An address with a view that doesn't exist opens the Board - Search, filters, sort and grouping carry over from view to view (TB-132) - Clicking a card, row, bar or calendar entry opens the item's panel

title: View the Work List
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see the contract's work in one place so that I can follow what the Independent Contractor is working on, what's mine to do, and what is waiting for my review.
ac: - The Work tab is the contract's default tab and shows the work full width — the same list the Independent Contractor and Hireable admin see - Board view is the default; List, Calendar, Timeline and Workload views show the same items (TB-131) - List view is a dense table — Name, Status, Assignee, Work type, Priority, Start, Due, Effort, Progress and Updated — grouped into collapsible sections (by status unless grouped otherwise) - Every item has a number (#12) that never changes, even when it is renamed - A line under the view switch sums the list: the trial day, the Trial Fit Score, how many items are done, in review and overdue - Tasks from the signed offer show what the offer set of them with a lock, in their panel and in the List; trying to change one says it was agreed in the signed offer (TB-077) - An item whose due date has passed and isn't completed shows Overdue in words, not only in red - An item waiting on unfinished work shows Blocked - An item sent back shows Changes requested until it is resubmitted - Items in review sit in the In review column and open from their card; a Review button in the header opens the first one waiting - Deleted items are left out of every view, count and score (TB-141)

title: Add a Task
story: As a Team Builder, I want to add work to the contract so that I can hand over new tasks as they come up.
ac: - Add task in the header opens a form with the name, assignee, work type, due date, effort and description; the new item then opens in its panel - Every board column and list group has a quick Add task row that inherits the column's value (the assignee, work type or priority it's grouped by); under status grouping it is on To do only - Quick add: Enter adds the item and keeps the field open for the next; Enter on an empty field closes it; Escape throws the draft away; clicking elsewhere adds what was typed; switching to another window keeps the draft - A day on the calendar can be added to directly — the new item is due that day (TB-137) - The name is required; a new item starts in To do, gets the next number (#13) and is assigned to the Independent Contractor unless another assignee is chosen - The Independent Contractor is notified when work is assigned to them: New task added - Only the Team Builder adds work, and only on a full-time or part-time contract: a trial's tasks are the ones agreed in its signed offer, so a trial has no Add task and takes no new work, in the app or through the API - An item that can't be saved disappears again with the reason and a Retry that adds it once

title: Comment on a Task
story: As a Team Builder, I want to comment on a task so that I can discuss the work with the Independent Contractor right where it happens.
ac: - The task details panel has a comment box under its activity feed - Either side can comment on any task, whatever its status, while the contract is live - Comments read as a comment thread, not a chat: each in its own box with the author's photo, name and time above the text, in time order with the task's history - The Independent Contractor is notified of each new comment, and the notification opens the task on its comments; more comments on the same task while that notification is unread update it instead of adding another - An empty comment can't be posted - An ended contract is read-only — its comments stay visible but no new ones can be added

title: Approve Task
story: As a Team Builder, I want to approve a task the Independent Contractor has submitted for review so that it is marked Done and counts toward their trial performance.
ac: - Approve is available on tasks In review — from the task details panel, the Review button on its row, or by dragging its card to Done in Board view - Approving moves the task to Done - Done is final: an approved task can't be edited, moved, or deleted - The Independent Contractor is notified: Task approved - The approval is recorded in the task's activity feed with who approved it and when - Done trial tasks feed the Trial Fit Score's Performance (Done trial tasks ÷ all trial tasks) - When every trial task is Done, the trial closes early instead of running to its end date - When the trial closes (every trial task Done, or its end date) or the contract ends, the activity tracker stops on the final streak - On a full-time or part-time contract the tracker keeps running when nothing is open, since the Team Builder can add the next task

title: Request Changes on a Task
story: As a Team Builder, I want to request changes on a task in review with a note so that the Independent Contractor knows what to fix before resubmitting.
ac: - Request changes is available on tasks In review — from the task details panel, the Review button on its row, or by dragging its card back to In progress in Board view - A note is required — Request changes can't be sent without one - The task moves back to In progress and shows the note as Changes requested until it is resubmitted - The Independent Contractor is notified: Changes requested on a task, with the note - When the Independent Contractor resubmits, the task returns to In review - The request and its note are recorded in the task's activity feed - Once a trial is over, Request changes is no longer available — the Independent Contractor couldn't make the changes; the Team Builder approves the task or leaves it for the evaluation

title: Set Due Dates and Priority
story: As a Team Builder, I want to set due dates and priorities on tasks so that the Independent Contractor knows what is due when and what matters most.
ac: - Due date and priority (Low / Medium / High) are optional on every task - The Team Builder sets or changes a task's due date and priority until the task is Done — except on a task from the signed offer, whose due date and priority stay as agreed (TB-077); the Independent Contractor sees them but can't change them - Agreed tasks start with the due dates from the offer's due weeks, counted in working weeks from the start date — on a trial, capped at its end date - Due date and priority show in the Due and Priority columns of the List view - A task whose due date has passed and isn't Done shows Overdue — a task due today isn't overdue yet - A Done task's due date and priority can't be changed

title: View Contract & Payment Tab
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view the contract terms and payment history for an Independent Contractor in the Contract & Payment tab so that I can review what was agreed upon and track financial activity during the trial.
ac: \* Tab shows: agreed job role, trial duration, start and end dates, agreed budget, payment schedule, and escrow status \* Payment history shows all transactions with: date, amount, type, and status \* Payment is held in escrow during the trial \* Tab is read-only — no editing available from this view

title: View Evaluation History
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view all submitted evaluations in the Evaluation tab so that I can reference past assessments for the Independent Contractor.
ac: \* Evaluation tab shows all evaluations submitted for the Independent Contractor \* Each entry shows: date submitted, star rating, and written feedback \* Finalized TFP score is shown after evaluation is submitted \* View is read-only — evaluations cannot be edited after submission \* Empty state shown if no evaluation has been submitted yet

title: Send Evaluation
story: As a Team Builder, I want to submit a post-trial evaluation for an Independent Contractor after the trial ends so that I can formally assess their performance and finalize their Trial Fit Score.
ac: \* Send Evaluation opens once the trial is over — the day after its last day, or once every trial task is approved — and is due within 5 days of the last day: the Team Builder is reminded the day before, and it shows as overdue after \* Button is greyed out and disabled during an active trial \* Evaluation form includes: star rating, written feedback, and overall recommendation \* Team Builder cannot submit the evaluation without completing all required fields \* Submitted evaluation is sent to the Independent Contractor as a notification \* Submitting it makes the Trial Fit Score final: the Phase 4 score (Evaluation weight 25%) is frozen as it stands, and nothing later — a late approval, the work after a conversion, a review of the role — changes it \* Submitting it pays the trial's escrow out to the Independent Contractor, less anything a dispute is holding; if 5 days pass after the last day with no evaluation and no dispute, the escrow pays out on its own \* While items are still waiting on review, the form says so — approve them first, since the score is final once sent \* End contract and Hire buttons unlock after evaluation is submitted — Hire offers the Independent Contractor a full-time or part-time role \* Past evaluations are viewable in the Evaluation tab

title: End Contract
story: As a Team Builder, I want to formally end the trial contract after submitting my evaluation so that I can close the engagement and release the escrowed payment to the Independent Contractor.
ac: - How the contract ends depends on where it is in its lifecycle, and each way is confirmed first - Before its first day (a signed trial, or a full-time or part-time role not started yet): Cancel contract — nothing was worked, so nothing is owed; a trial's escrow goes back to the Team Builder, and the Independent Contractor is told - During the trial, and until the evaluation has been submitted, End contract is greyed out and disabled - After the trial's evaluation (deciding what's next, or while a post-trial offer is out): End contract releases whatever the escrow still holds to the Independent Contractor and withdraws a post-trial offer still out; the Independent Contractor is notified with what was paid - On a running full-time or part-time role, the Team Builder chooses: Give notice — the role carries on, and is paid, for 30 days (full-time) or 14 days (part-time), as the services agreement says, then ends on its own after its last day — or End today, paying the Independent Contractor through the notice's last day (in lieu of notice) - Notice given shows on both sides: the header status reads Ends <date>, the Overview says who gave it and when, and the term runs to that date; the Team Builder can withdraw notice they gave before its last day, and the role carries on - When notice runs out, the contract ends on its own, the last pay (pro rata to the last day) is recorded and both sides are told - End contract waits while a dispute is holding money — the trial's escrow, or a role's pay — until it is resolved; notice can still be given - Ending is final: nothing reopens the contract, and Hire is no longer available - File a Dispute stays available as the alternative to ending while there's something to dispute: on a trial, from its last day until the evaluation pays out the escrow, before End contract unlocks; on a full-time or part-time role, for as long as it runs - An ended contract moves to the inactive state on the All Independents list, and its review period stops moving

title: Hire After the Trial
story: As a Team Builder, I want to hire an Independent Contractor full-time or part-time after their trial so that I can keep working with them when I'm satisfied with their trial performance.
ac: - Hire button is only available after the post-trial evaluation has been submitted — before that it is greyed out and disabled - Clicking Hire opens the post-trial offer form, pre-filled with the Independent Contractor's details, where the Team Builder chooses Full-time or Part-time — it opens on the one the evaluation recommended (Hire full-time or Hire part-time) - Full-time: the Team Builder sets the monthly salary, the start date, and any exclusive benefits - Part-time: the Team Builder sets the monthly rate, the hours per week, and the start date — no exclusive benefits - Only one post-trial offer can be open at a time — Hire is unavailable while an offer is waiting on an answer - The Team Builder can withdraw an open offer; a withdrawn offer can no longer be accepted - Submitted offer appears in Sent Offers, and the Independent Contractor is notified of the full-time or part-time offer - If the Independent Contractor declines, the Team Builder is notified, with their reason if they gave one - When the offer is accepted, any escrow still held for the trial is released to the Independent Contractor, and the contract continues as full-time or part-time - After the conversion, the Trial Fit Score is frozen at its final value and shown read-only on the Full-Time and Part-Time Dashboard - A declined or withdrawn offer returns the contract to its decision: the Team Builder can send a new offer or end the contract - The contract's Overview says where the decision stands: hire or end, the offer out (with Withdraw offer), a declined offer (with its reason) or a withdrawn one - An offer can't be sent on a contract that has ended - The start date can be today or later; if the Independent Contractor hasn't answered by the start date, the offer expires on its own: it can no longer be accepted, both sides are told, Sent Offers shows it as Expired, and the contract is back at its decision so a new offer (with a later start) can be sent - Pay on the role can never be back-dated to days before the offer was accepted

title: File a Dispute
story: As a Team Builder, I want to file a dispute as soon as the trial ends so that I can raise concerns about payment or performance before closing the engagement.
ac: - File a Dispute button is available immediately when the trial ends — no evaluation required; until then it stays in view, disabled, saying the day filing opens - Dispute form requires: reason, description and amount in question (a real sum no bigger than what's at stake); screenshots and PDFs (up to 6, 10 MB each) and a link are optional - The dispute can't be submitted until every required field is complete - Filing opens it as a case: the Independent Contractor is notified and has 5 days to respond — if they don't, it closes in the filer's favor - The filer goes straight to the case page; the dispute also lists under Sent Disputes as Pending - The amount in question stays in escrow while the case is open - The amount is checked again when the dispute is saved, and a refusal says why (a case already open, the timing, or the amount) - One dispute per chapter: the trial and the full-time or part-time role it became each get their own, so a dispute filed (or withdrawn) about the trial doesn't stop one about the role; only one case can be open at a time

title: Send Message to Independent Contractor
story: As a Team Builder, I want to send a message to an Independent Contractor directly from their trial dashboard so that I can communicate with them without leaving their profile.
ac: \* Send Message button is visible in the dashboard header at all times during an active trial \* Clicking Send Message opens the messaging interface with the Independent Contractor pre-selected \* Team Builder can compose and send a message without leaving the trial dashboard \* Empty message cannot be sent

title: View Full-Time and Part-Time Dashboard
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view the full-time or part-time dashboard of an Independent Contractor so that I can monitor their ongoing work, tasks, and contract details in one place.
ac: - Dashboard header shows: Independent Contractor name, role, and contract status badges (Full-Time or Part-Time, Active) - A contract signed ahead of its start date shows Starts <date> in place of its status until that day, and the activity tracker starts counting from then rather than showing the Independent Contractor as Unresponsive - Summary stats bar shows: Tasks count, Done count, Waiting for review count, and the contract start date - On a contract that converted from a trial, the Trial Fit Score widget shows the trial's final TFP score — read-only, does not update - On a contract hired directly with no trial, there is no trial score — the widget shows the match percentage at hire instead - Tasks are never locked — the Team Builder can add tasks at any time while the contract is active - Navigation tabs visible: Tasks, Contract & Payment, Evaluation - Tasks tab is the default view when the dashboard loads - Send Message button is visible in the header at all times - File a Dispute button is visible in the header at all times - Clicking Contract & Payment tab shows contract terms and payment history - Clicking Evaluation tab shows all submitted evaluations - A contract that converted from a trial keeps the trial as its first chapter: its dates, escrow, final Trial Fit Score and evaluation on Contract & Payment, and the trial's evaluation apart from the role's reviews - The summary shows Full-time or Part-time since its start date; pay is recorded on the last day of each month (pro rata for a part month) and Contract & Payment shows the next payday and amount, and the benefits the signed offer actually included - File a Dispute stays available for as long as the contract runs — after a conversion it's about the pay, up to a month's pay - Notice given by either side shows as Ends <date> in the header and on the Overview until the role ends

title: View Task List (Full-Time / Part-Time)
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view the task list of a full-time or part-time Independent Contractor so that I can follow their ongoing work.
ac: - Tasks tab shows the contract's shared task list — the same list the Independent Contractor sees - List view is the default, grouped into collapsible sections by status (To do, In progress, In review, Done) with columns Task, Due, Priority, Added by, and Status; Board view is also available - New tasks can be added at any time while the contract is active; the first tasks from the signed offer, if it had any, stay as agreed (TB-077) - New tasks added by either side appear in the list immediately - Rows show Overdue and Changes requested where they apply - Tasks In review show a Review button on the row - Clicking a task opens the task details panel - An ended contract's task list is read-only

title: Break a Task into Subtasks
story: As a Team Builder, I want to break a task into subtasks so that larger pieces of work have clear, checkable steps.
ac: - Subtasks are added as a checklist in the task details panel - Either side can add subtasks to a task that isn't Done - Only the Independent Contractor ticks subtasks off; the Team Builder sees which ones are ticked - Ticking a subtask counts as working on tasks that day on the activity heatmap (light green) - Subtasks work the same on trial, full-time, and part-time contracts

title: Edit or Delete a Task
story: As a Team Builder, I want to edit or delete tasks I added so that the task list stays accurate as the work changes.
ac: - The Team Builder can edit the title and description of tasks they added until they are In review or Done - Tasks from the signed offer keep what the offer set of them: neither side changes their name, description, due date or priority — the fields the trial post's task plan carries, even one left blank — or who does them, or deletes them, in the app or through the API; what they are was settled in the proposal, before the offer (TB-106). Each shows a lock where it would be edited, in the panel and the List, and trying one says it was agreed in the signed offer - Everything the offer didn't set is worked like any other task's: status, start date, effort, work type, tags, dependencies, subtasks and comments, under each side's usual rights - Finishing one keeps its agreed due date; its history says when it finished - A trial's agreement holds while the contract is a trial; once it becomes a full-time or part-time role, the tasks the trial left unfinished are the role's work like any other, and what it finished stays read-only as the trial's chapter (TB-148) - The Team Builder can delete a task they added only if it isn't from the signed offer and isn't In review or Done - The Independent Contractor doesn't add, edit, or delete tasks — they break them into subtasks - Done is final: an approved task can't be edited, moved, or deleted - A deleted task disappears from the list for both sides - An ended contract is read-only — nothing can be edited or deleted

title: Get Notified About Task Reviews
story: As a Team Builder, I want to be notified when the Independent Contractor submits a task for review so that their work doesn't sit waiting for me.
ac: - When the Independent Contractor submits a task for review, the Team Builder gets a notification (e.g. 'Juan sent a task for review') - Clicking the notification opens the contract with that task open in the task details panel - The Independent Contractor's optional note for the reviewer shows on the task - The dashboard's review banner and Waiting for review count include the task while it is In review - Notifications work the same on trial, full-time, and part-time contracts

title: Track Overdue Tasks
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see which tasks are overdue so that I can follow up on late work.
ac: - A task is Overdue when its due date has passed and it isn't Done — a task due today isn't overdue yet - Overdue shows on the task's row - Overdue isn't a status and can't be set by hand — it is worked out from the due date and status - Overdue clears once the task is Done or its due date is moved to a later day - Tasks without a due date are never overdue - The Independent Contractor's card on All Independents shows the number of Overdue tasks in red

title: View Task Activity
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see a task's activity so that I know what happened to it and when.
ac: - The task details panel shows one activity feed with the task's history and its comments, in time order - History covers when the task was added and by whom, status changes, submissions for review, approvals, and requested changes with their notes - Each entry shows who did it and when - Activity entries can't be edited or removed - The feed stays visible on Done tasks and on ended contracts

title: Review Tasks from the Dashboard Banner
story: As a Team Builder, I want a banner on the dashboard when tasks are waiting for my review so that I can act on them straight away.
ac: - When one or more tasks are In review, a banner at the top of the dashboard says how many are waiting - The banner's action opens a task waiting for review in the task details panel - From the panel the Team Builder can Approve or Request changes - The banner updates as tasks are reviewed and disappears once none are In review - The banner shows on trial, full-time, and part-time dashboards

title: Approve Task (Full-Time / Part-Time)
story: As a Team Builder, I want to approve a task a full-time or part-time Independent Contractor has submitted for review so that it is marked Done.
ac: - Approve is available on tasks In review — from the task details panel, the Review button on its row, or by dragging its card to Done in Board view - Approving moves the task to Done - Done is final: an approved task can't be edited, moved, or deleted - The Independent Contractor is notified: Task approved - The approval is recorded in the task's activity feed - The contract's progress (share of tasks Done) updates - On a contract that converted from a trial, the Trial Fit Score stays frozen — approvals no longer change it - New tasks can be added at any time to follow on from finished ones

title: Request Changes on a Task (Full-Time / Part-Time)
story: As a Team Builder, I want to request changes on a full-time or part-time Independent Contractor's task in review, with a note, so that they know what to fix before resubmitting.
ac: - Request changes is available on tasks In review — from the task details panel, the Review button on its row, or by dragging its card back to In progress in Board view - A note is required — Request changes can't be sent without one - The task moves back to In progress and shows the note as Changes requested until it is resubmitted - The Independent Contractor is notified: Changes requested on a task, with the note - When the Independent Contractor resubmits, the task returns to In review - The request and its note are recorded in the task's activity feed

title: Move Work on the Board
story: As a Team Builder, I want to move cards on the board so that I can approve work, move my own items along and keep the order that matters.
ac: - Dragging a card from In review to Done approves it; back to In progress requests changes and asks for the note first (the panel opens on it) — without a note nothing changes - The Team Builder moves their own items and unassigned ones between To do, In progress and Done freely — they never go through In review - The Team Builder can't move the Independent Contractor's work between To do, In progress and In review — hovering a card says why - Columns a card can't go to don't take the drop, and say why while dragging - Grouped by assignee, work type or priority, dropping a card on another column changes that value - With Manual sort, a card lands where it's dropped and the order is kept in every view (TB-142) - Keyboard: Alt+Shift+Left/Right moves a focused card to the next column it can go to; the card's ⋯ menu offers Move to, Move up, Move down, Move to top and Move to bottom - Every move shows at once and is saved; if it can't be saved the card goes back with the reason (TB-144) - A move notifies the Independent Contractor the same way Approve and Request changes do

title: View Contract & Payment Tab
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view the full-time or part-time contract terms, pay, exclusive benefits, and payment history so that I can keep track of the full financial engagement.
ac: - Full-time: tab shows agreed job role, contract start date, base salary, exclusive benefits breakdown, and payment schedule - Exclusive benefits listed separately: Health Insurance, Government Contribution, Internet Allowance, Learning & Development Allowance - Part-time: tab shows agreed job role, contract start date, monthly rate, hours per week, and payment schedule — part-time contracts have no exclusive benefits - Payment history shows all transactions with: date, amount, type, and status - Tab is read-only — no editing available from this view

title: Send Evaluation
story: As a Team Builder, I want to submit a performance evaluation for a full-time or part-time Independent Contractor at any time so that I can provide ongoing feedback throughout the engagement.
ac: - Send Evaluation button is available at any time during an active full-time or part-time contract — not gated by an end date, but not before it starts or once it has ended - Evaluation form includes: star rating, written feedback, and overall recommendation - Team Builder cannot submit the evaluation without completing all required fields - Submitted evaluation is sent to the Independent Contractor as a notification - Submitted evaluation appears in the Evaluation tab immediately

title: View Evaluation History
story: As a Team Builder, I want to view all submitted evaluations in the Evaluation tab so that I can reference past assessments for the Independent Contractor.
ac: - Evaluation tab shows all evaluations submitted for the Independent Contractor during the full-time or part-time engagement - Each entry shows: date submitted, star rating, and written feedback - Entries are sorted by most recent - View is read-only — evaluations cannot be edited after submission - Empty state shown if no evaluation has been submitted yet

title: File a Dispute
story: As a Team Builder, I want to file a dispute at any point during the full-time or part-time engagement so that I can raise concerns about payment or performance.
ac: - File a Dispute button is available at any time during an active full-time or part-time contract — not before its first day (it says the day filing opens) and not once the contract has ended (it says it can't be disputed any more); the same rule is checked again when the dispute is saved - Dispute form requires: reason, description and amount in question (a real sum no bigger than what's at stake); screenshots and PDFs (up to 6, 10 MB each) and a link are optional - The dispute can't be submitted until every required field is complete - Filing opens it as a case: the Independent Contractor is notified and has 5 days to respond — if they don't, it closes in the filer's favor - The filer goes straight to the case page; the dispute also lists under Sent Disputes as Pending - The amount in question stays in escrow while the case is open - On a contract that converted from a trial, filing stays available once the trial's escrow is paid out: the dispute is about the pay, up to a month's pay - On a full-time or part-time role there is no escrow, so the amount in question (up to a month's pay) is kept back from the next payday while the case is open, and the Independent Contractor is told their pay is held. When it closes, what was kept back is paid on, refunded to the company, or split as agreed; a refund bigger than what was kept back comes off the following pay - One dispute per chapter: the trial and the full-time or part-time role it became each get their own, so a dispute filed (or withdrawn) about the trial doesn't stop one about the role; only one case can be open at a time - End contract waits until the case closes; notice can still be given

title: Send Message to Independent Contractor
story: As a Team Builder, I want to send a message to an Independent Contractor directly from their full-time or part-time dashboard so that I can communicate with them without leaving their profile.
ac: - Send Message button is visible in the dashboard header at all times - Clicking Send Message opens the messaging interface with the Independent Contractor pre-selected - Team Builder can compose and send a message without leaving the full-time or part-time dashboard - Empty message cannot be sent

title: View Payments Overview
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see a summary of my total spending across all contracts so that I can quickly understand my overall payment activity on the platform.
ac: - Payments page shows a summary card with: total amount spent across all contracts - Summary is updated in real time as new transactions are recorded - Clicking a transaction navigates to the transaction detail view

title: View Transaction History
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see a full list of all payment transactions across all my contracts so that I can track my complete spending history in one place.
ac: - Transaction History shows all recorded payment activity across all contracts - Each row shows: date, contract name, Independent Contractor name, transaction type, amount, and status - Transaction types: Payment Deposited, Payment Released, Payment Refunded - Default sort by most recent - Pagination applied - Empty state shown if no transactions exist

title: Filter Transactions
story: As a Team Builder, I want to filter my transactions by contract, status, and date range so that I can narrow down records to find what I am looking for.
ac: - Filter options: by contract name, by status (Deposited, Released, Refunded), by date range - Filters can be combined - Active filters are visually indicated - Clearing filters restores the full list

title: Search Transactions
story: As a Team Builder, I want to search my transactions so that I can quickly locate a specific payment record.

title: View Transaction Detail
story: As a Team Builder, I want to open a specific transaction to view its full details so that I can review the breakdown of a specific payment.
ac: - Clicking a transaction opens the detail view - Shows: date, contract name, Independent Contractor name, transaction type, amount, and status - Read-only view

title: View Sent Disputes
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see all disputes I have filed across all contracts in one list so that I can monitor the status of each dispute.
ac: - Sent Disputes lists every dispute the Team Builder has filed across all contracts; Received lists the ones filed against them - Each row shows: date filed, contract name and reason, the other party, amount, who the case is waiting on (with the time left on their turn), and status (Pending / Resolved / Rejected / Withdrawn) - Rows waiting on this person say so and open with Respond; every row opens the case page - Default sort by most recent; search and a status filter narrow the list - Empty state shown if no disputes have been filed

title: View Dispute Detail
story: As a Team Builder, I want to open a specific dispute to view its full details and status updates so that I can stay informed on the process check outcome.
ac: - Each dispute opens as a case page, from the list, the contract or any notification about it - A banner says whose turn it is and until when ("It's your turn to respond — by Tue 30 Sep, 9:00 AM (5 days left)"), what happens if the time runs out, or how the case ended - A strip shows where each side stands — the company, the independent and Hireable support — with the one whose turn it is highlighted - One timeline shows everything in order, each entry marked with who it's from: the filing (reason, amount, description, files), each side's responses and additions, support's questions and deadline changes, settlement proposals and answers, and the outcome - Screenshots open full size and PDFs open in a new tab; both sides and support see the same files - The side panel shows the amount in question and where it stands, the contract's payments — escrow funded, paid to the independent, refunded to the company, still pending in escrow — and the contract, with a link to it - The Independent Contractor and Hireable support read the same case; nothing on it can be edited after it's sent

title: Withdraw Dispute
story: As a Team Builder, I want to withdraw a pending dispute so that I can cancel it if the issue has been resolved or I have changed my mind.
ac: - Withdraw dispute is in the case page's header, for the party who filed it, while the case is open - Confirmation prompt shown before withdrawing - Dispute status changes to Withdrawn and an open settlement proposal is closed with it - Hireable admin sees the withdrawal as new activity and the Independent Contractor is notified that the dispute has been withdrawn - Once withdrawn, a new dispute cannot be filed for the same chapter of the contract (the trial, or the role it became)
