title: Work Views over One List
story: As a Team Builder, I want Board, List, Calendar, Timeline and Workload views of the same work so that I can plan and follow it the way each question needs.
ac: - Board: a column per status (or per assignee, work type or priority), each with its count and total effort, a quick add row, and cards showing the number, work type, due date, priority, effort, Blocked, Changes requested, subtask progress, comments, tags and assignee - List: a dense, editable table grouped the same way, with sortable column headers and collapsible groups; a group's heading stays in view — under the column headers while its rows scroll past, and at the left edge when the table scrolls sideways - Calendar: the month, with each item on its dates (TB-137) - Timeline: each item as a bar across its dates, with dependencies drawn (TB-138) - Workload: who has how much work on which days (TB-140) - Every view reads the one list — a change made in one shows in every other at once, and after a reload - Each view has its own empty state: no work yet, nothing matching the filters, or nothing scheduled - The views stay quick with hundreds of items: long lists render as they scroll

title: Search, Filter, Sort and Group Work
story: As a Team Builder, I want to narrow and arrange the work so that I can find what matters without losing my place.
ac: - Search matches the name, description, tags and #number; every word must match, ignoring case and accents - Filters: status, assignee (Juan, Alex, Unassigned), work type, priority (including none), due date (overdue, today, this week, this month, no due date), tags, blocked only, and the delete - Filters combine: AND across kinds, OR within one kind; filter menus stay open while several values are ticked - Each active filter shows as a chip that removes it; Clear all removes every filter and the search - Sort: Manual (the default), Due date, Start date, Priority, Effort, Name, Created, Last updated — ascending or descending; items without the value go last - Group (Board, List, Timeline): Status, Assignee, Work type, Priority, or none - The toolbar shows how many items match out of the total - All of it lives in the address: it carries across views, survives a reload, and Back restores the earlier set; an invalid value in the address reads as the default

title: Assign Work
story: As a Team Builder, I want to assign each item to the Independent Contractor, to myself, or to nobody yet so that everyone knows whose work it is.
ac: - New items are assigned to the Independent Contractor unless another assignee is chosen - Assignee is changed from the panel, the list's Assignee column, or by dropping the card on a person's column when grouped by assignee - Assigning an item to the Independent Contractor notifies them - The Team Builder's own items and unassigned ones don't go through review: the Team Builder moves them to Done directly, and reopens them if needed - Only the Independent Contractor's items count toward the Trial Fit Score, the trial's early close and the dispute process check - Items agreed in the signed offer stay assigned to the Independent Contractor it was made to, while the agreement holds (TB-077) - Only To do and In progress items can be reassigned

title: Estimate Effort
story: As a Team Builder, I want to give each item a relative effort so that I can see how big the work is and how it is spread.
ac: - Effort is a whole number from 0 to 999, set from the presets 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 or typed, and can be cleared - It is described as a relative estimate of the amount of work required — not hours - Cards show the effort; board columns and list groups total it - Milestones have no effort - The Team Builder sets it on every task, including ones from the signed offer, which doesn't set effort (TB-077); the Independent Contractor sees effort but doesn't set it

title: Classify Work by Type
story: As a Team Builder, I want to say what kind of work each item is so that the list reads at a glance and can be filtered and grouped.
ac: - Work types: Task (the default), Milestone, Design, Development, Marketing, Content, Research, Review, Meeting, Admin, Operations, Other — each with its own icon and name - A milestone is a checkpoint on a single date: it has a due date, no start and no effort, and draws as a diamond on the timeline; turning an item into a milestone clears its start and effort and says so - Work type is set from the panel or the list, filtered on, and grouped by

title: Schedule Work with Start and Due Dates
story: As a Team Builder, I want to give items a start date, a due date, both or neither so that the calendar, timeline and workload show when the work happens.
ac: - An item can have a start and a due date, only one of them, or neither (it is then unscheduled) - Dates are calendar days: they read the same in every time zone and across daylight-saving changes - The due date can't be before the start date; a new due date can't be in the past; on a trial nothing can start or be due after its last day — days that break a rule can't be picked, and a save that would break one is refused with the reason - Dates are set from the panel, the list, by dragging on the calendar or the timeline, or with the keyboard on the timeline - The dates follow the work: moving an item to In progress sets its start to that day, unless it already starts earlier or is overdue; approving it (or marking the Team Builder's own item Done) sets its due date to that day, and its history keeps the due date it had; milestones keep their date - Completed items aren't overdue

title: Calendar View
story: As a Team Builder, I want a month calendar of the work so that I can see what falls when and move it.
ac: - Weeks start on Sunday, as the date pickers do; today is marked in words as well as colour - An item with a start and a due spans those days (split at the week's end and marked where it carries on); one with only a due date sits on it; one with only a start sits on its start as Starts; a milestone sits on its date - Each day shows up to three lanes, then +N more, which lists everything on that day - Items with no dates are listed beside the month as Unscheduled - Dragging an item to another day moves it and keeps its length; dragging an unscheduled item onto a day makes it due that day; days a rule rules out don't take the drop - A day's + adds an item due that day - Previous, Next and Today move between months, and the month is kept in the address - On a phone the month reads as a list of the days with work on them

title: Timeline View
story: As a Team Builder, I want a timeline of the work so that I can see its schedule and dependencies and adjust them directly.
ac: - Day, Week and Month scales, with a Today marker and weekends shaded; the scale is kept in the address - Each item is a row with a bar across its dates: a span, a one-day marker for a due date alone, an open-ended stub for a start alone, a diamond for a milestone; items with no dates show No dates and Schedule - Dragging a bar moves it and keeps its length; dragging its left end changes the start, its right end the due date; a change that breaks a rule turns red, says why and isn't saved; Escape cancels - Keyboard: with a bar focused, Left/Right moves it a day, Shift+Left/Right changes the due date, Alt+Shift+Left/Right the start; it saves when the keys stop, on Enter or on leaving the bar - The Independent Contractor changes only the start of their own To do and In progress items — the left end, or Alt+Shift+Left/Right — and the hint above the timeline says so; clicking any bar opens its item (IN-087) - Lines run from each item to the work that waits on it; a line is dashed red when the waiting work starts before what it waits on is due - Rows follow the toolbar's sort and grouping

title: Track Dependencies
story: As a Team Builder, I want to say which work waits on which so that blocked work is visible and the order makes sense.
ac: - From the panel, the Team Builder adds what any open item waits on by searching for it by name or #number, and removes it again; the Independent Contractor does the same on their own items (IN-087) - The panel lists what the item waits on and what it is blocking - An item waiting on work that isn't completed shows Blocked on its card, row and panel; deleted work doesn't block - An item can't wait on itself, twice on the same item, on deleted work, or on work that already waits on it — directly or down a chain; the message names the loop (#4 → #10 → #4) - The timeline draws the dependencies (TB-138); the filter Blocked only lists blocked work

title: Workload View
story: As a Team Builder, I want to see how much work each person has on each day so that I can spread it sensibly.
ac: - A row each for the Independent Contractor, the Team Builder and Unassigned; a column for each day of a two- or four-week window, weekends shaded and today marked - Measured in Effort by default, or in Items (how many are in flight each day) - An item's effort is spread evenly over the working days from its start to its due date; an item with only a due date counts on that day, only a start on its start; items with no dates are listed under No dates - Work that falls before or after the window is totalled at its edges; dated items without an effort estimate are listed - Completed items count only when Include done is ticked - Each cell opens the items that make it up, with each one's share - Effort is relative and nobody's capacity is recorded, so nothing is flagged as over capacity — how the numbers are worked out is written beside the grid - The window, measure and Include done are kept in the address

title: Archive and Restore Work
story: As a Team Builder, I want to archive work that's no longer needed instead of deleting it so that nothing is lost and a mistake can be undone.
ac: - Delete is in the item's ⋯ menu and panel; a confirmation offers Undo - Deleted items leave every view, count, total, workload and score, and don't block other work - Filter › Show deleted instead lists them; Restore brings one back - Agreed items (while their agreement holds, TB-077), and the Independent Contractor's work once it has been sent for review or approved, can't be deleted - Nothing is permanently deleted from the list

title: Order Work by Hand
story: As a Team Builder, I want to set the order of the work so that the most important items come first.
ac: - With Manual sort, the Team Builder drags cards within a column (or between columns) to where they belong - Keyboard: Alt+Shift+Up/Down on a focused card or row, or Move up, Move down, Move to top and Move to bottom in its ⋯ menu - The order is one list shared by every view and saved - The Independent Contractor sees the order but doesn't change it - Under another sort, dragging within a column doesn't reorder, and the board says so

title: Contract Overview Tab
story: As a Team Builder, I want the contract's summary on its own tab so that the Work tab can use the full width.
ac: - Tabs: Work (the default, and what older links with ?tab=tasks open), Overview, Contract & Payment, Evaluation - Message and File a dispute stay in the header row on every tab - Overview opens with a banner for anything waiting on the Team Builder — work sent for review (with Review, which opens it), or a trial that ended without an evaluation (with Send evaluation) - Then the contract at a glance: role, start date, the trial's day and working days left, end date, pay and hours - Progress: the share of items done, effort done, trial tasks done on a trial, how many are in review and overdue, and the split by status - Needs attention: work waiting on their review and anything overdue; Coming up: open work due in the next two weeks, by day, with who has it; Recent changes: the latest things that happened on any item, comments included — every item opens in the Work tab - Beside them: the Trial Fit Score or Match at hire, the activity log, the evaluation card and the contract & payment card - All of it is worked out from the contract's items, so it always matches the Work tab

title: Saving Work Reliably
story: As a Team Builder, I want every change to be saved or clearly refused so that I never see a change that didn't happen, or lose one that did.
ac: - A change shows at once while it saves, and settles once saved; if it can't be saved it is taken back, with a message saying why and, where it helps, Retry or Undo - Two people changing different fields of the same item both keep their change; a change to a field someone else changed first is refused — it says who, and Use mine saves it over theirs - A status change made on an out-of-date screen is refused rather than applied to the wrong state - Changes to one item are saved in order; when one fails, the ones queued behind it are dropped and the user is told - If the browser can't save (storage full or blocked), nothing is changed and the message says so - If the saved data can't be read, it is kept (a copy is made) and never written over; the page explains and offers Try again and Reset demo data - Who may do what is checked on every save, not only by hiding buttons — the same rules refuse a change made any other way - Messages explain the problem in plain words; no technical errors are shown

title: Respond to a Dispute
story: As a Team Builder, I want to answer a dispute on my turn, with the screenshots that back me up, so that the case is decided on both sides of the story.
ac: - When a dispute is filed against the Team Builder, or Hireable support asks them a question, it's their turn: they have 5 days to respond - A response carries text (required), screenshots and PDFs (up to 6, 10 MB each) and an optional link; sending it hands the case to Hireable support for review - A reminder is sent when one day is left; if the time runs out with no response, the case closes in the Independent Contractor's favor and the money moves as a ruling would - When it isn't their turn they can still add information for support, with files; it doesn't change whose turn it is - the Independent Contractor is notified of every response and addition, and can read it on the case

title: Settle a Dispute
story: As a Team Builder, I want to settle a dispute with the Independent Contractor by splitting the amount in question so that we can close it without waiting for a ruling.
ac: - Either side can propose a settlement while the case is open: how the amount in question splits between a refund to the company and a release to the independent - Quick splits (all to one side, half each) and two amounts that fill each other in; the two parts must add up to the amount in question - The Independent Contractor is notified and sees the proposal on the case with Accept and Decline; a newer proposal from either side replaces the open one - Accepting — confirmed first — closes the case as Resolved by agreement and moves both parts straight away, never more than the escrow still holds - Declining keeps the case going and tells the proposer

title: View Dashboard Overview
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see a personalized dashboard when I log in, so that I can quickly get an overview of my account activity and know what to do next.
ac: - Dashboard loads upon login showing all key widgets - Displays active contracts, open tasks (IN-090), recent messages, and account setup progress - All widgets are clickable and navigate to relevant sections - Personalized greeting shown with Independent Contractor's name

title: View Marketing Banner
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see a marketing banner on my dashboard, so that I can stay informed about platform updates, promotions, or featured opportunities.
ac: - Marketing banner displayed prominently on dashboard - Banner can contain text, image, and CTA link - Banner is dismissible - Hidden if no active banner exists

title: Account Setup Checklist
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see a checklist showing my account setup progress (Verify Email, Answer Work Style Quiz, Setup Profile, Setup Payment Method, Apply to Role), so that I can complete my profile and become fully ready to be hired.
ac: - Checklist shows 5 steps: Verify Email, Answer Work Style Quiz, Setup Profile, Setup Payment Method, Apply to Role - Completed steps marked with checkmark - Each step is clickable and navigates to the relevant section - Checklist disappears or collapses once all steps are completed

title: View Active Contracts
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see my active contracts on my dashboard showing the company, contract type, and role, so that I can quickly access my ongoing engagements.
ac: - Active contracts widget shows all ongoing Trial, Full-Time, and Part-Time engagements - Each card shows company name, role, contract type, and days remaining or start date - Clicking a contract navigates to the relevant contract dashboard - Empty state shown if no active contracts

title: Quick Access to My Tasks
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want my open tasks on my dashboard, so that I can get straight to the work that needs me without going through my contracts first.
ac: - While a contract with a work list is live, the dashboard shows My tasks under the greeting: the contract's role and company, and how many of the Independent Contractor's tasks are To do, In progress and In review - It lists up to five of their own open tasks, most pressing first: sent back with changes, overdue, in progress, then To do by due date (undated last), then those waiting on the Team Builder's review - Each row shows the task's status, number and name, and why it's there: Changes requested, its due date (Overdue in red), or With the Team Builder for review - Clicking a row opens that task in its panel on the contract's Work tab; the arrow and "N more in the Work tab" open the Work tab filtered to their own tasks - Done, archived and other people's tasks aren't listed; with nothing open, it says they're all caught up - Without a live contract the card isn't shown

title: Quick Action Shortcuts
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see two quick action cards — Find Your Next Role (→ Roles) and Complete Your Profile (→ Profile) — so that I can navigate to the most important next steps directly from my dashboard.
ac: - Two quick action cards shown: Find Your Next Role (→ Roles) and Complete Your Profile (→ Profile) - Each card shows title, short description, and CTA button - Cards always visible on dashboard

title: Send Message
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to send messages to Team Builders, so that I can communicate about role opportunities, contracts, and tasks.
ac: - Independent Contractor can compose and send messages to Team Builders they have an active connection with - Message delivered in real time - Sent messages appear in conversation thread immediately - Empty message cannot be sent

title: Receive Message
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to receive messages from Team Builders, so that I can stay informed and respond to any communication related to my applications or contracts.
ac: - Independent Contractor receives messages from Team Builders in real time - New messages trigger a notification - Messages appear in correct conversation thread - Unread count updates automatically

title: Show Unread Indicator
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see an unread message indicator on my inbox, so that I know when I have new messages that need my attention.
ac: - Unread message count displayed on Messages nav icon - Count updates in real time - Count clears when conversation is opened

title: Search Messages
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to search through my messages, so that I can quickly find a specific conversation without scrolling through my entire inbox.
ac: - Search bar available within Messages module - Filters conversations by Team Builder name or keyword - Results update as user types - Empty state shown when no results match

title: Attach Files in Messages
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to attach files in my messages, so that I can share documents, portfolios, or deliverables with Team Builders directly in the chat.
ac: - File attachment button available in message composer - Supported types: PDF, DOC, DOCX, PNG, JPG (max 10MB) - Attached file previewed before sending - Recipient can download from message thread

title: Start / Join Call
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to start or join a call from within the messaging interface, so that I can communicate with Team Builders in real time without leaving the platform.
ac: - Call button available within an active conversation - Clicking initiates or joins a call session - Call interface includes mute, camera toggle, and end call - Notification sent to other party when call starts

title: Browse Roles
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to browse all available role listings, so that I can explore opportunities that match my skills and interests.
ac: \* Roles page displays all available and active role listings \* Each card shows: company logo, role title, type (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), budget/salary, experience level, and match percentage \* Results load with pagination at the bottom \* Pagination shows: Previous, page numbers, and Next \* Empty state shown if no listings are available \* Search bar available on Roles page — searches by role title, company name, or skills \* Results update dynamically as Independent Contractor types \* Clearing the search bar restores the full list \* Filter options: role type (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), experience level, budget/salary range \* Multiple filters can be applied simultaneously \* Active filters are visually indicated \* Clearing filters restores the full list \* Match percentage displayed on each role listing card \* Color coded: green (high), yellow (medium), red (low) \* Phase 1 (Work Style only) shown before trial \* Phase 2 (+ Role & Profile) updates when profile is complete \* Tooltip explains what the score is based on \* Clicking a role card opens the full role details \* Role details show: company info, role title, type, description, required skills, experience level, budget/salary, trial duration (if Trial), and hours per week (if Part-Time) — the pay, trial length or start, and experience in a facts strip under the title \* A Work style section shows the company's Workplace Tags beside the Independent Contractor's own, trait by trait, each marked In sync, Close, or Different, with a count of each — it replaces the old work-style chart \* On a trial role, a Trial tasks section lists the tasks the Team Builder set once the Independent Contractor is matched or invited; before that it says how many there are \* How hiring works shows the four steps: Apply, Interview, Proposal, then the paid trial or the offer \* Once applied, the role details link to the application instead of offering Apply again \* Apply button visible on role details page \* Match percentage prominently shown on role details page

title: Apply to Role
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to apply to a role listing, so that I can formally express my interest and be considered for the role by the Team Builder.
ac: \* Apply button available on role listing card and role details page \* Application submitted immediately upon clicking \* Independent Contractor cannot apply to the same role twice \* Team Builder is notified of the application \* Application appears in My Applications with Applied status

title: View All Applications
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see all the roles I've applied to in one list so that I can track where I am in the hiring process for each application.
ac: \* My Applications page shows all roles the Independent Contractor has applied to \* Each row shows: company logo, role title, type (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), date applied, current stage, and current status \* Pipeline stages and statuses per stage: \* Application Sent — no status \* Matched — no status \* Interview Requested — Awaiting Confirmation, Interview Confirmed, Interview Completed \* Proposal Requested — Awaiting Proposal, Proposal Submitted, Requested Revision by TB \* Offer Received — Awaiting Response, Offer Accepted, Declined \* Hired — Waiting to Start, Started, Contract Completed, Contract Terminated \* Clicking a row opens the full application detail view \* If an offer has been received, a Review Offer button is visible on the card \* Default sort by most recent \* Empty state shown if no applications exist

title: Accept Interview Invitation
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to accept an interview invitation from a Team Builder so that I can confirm my availability and move forward in the hiring process.
ac: \* Accept button is available when application stage is Interview Requested and status is Awaiting Confirmation \* Clicking Accept changes the status to Interview Confirmed \* Team Builder is notified that the interview has been accepted \* A meeting link is shown to the Independent Contractor after accepting \* Accept button is hidden once status moves past Awaiting Confirmation

title: Join Interview Call
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to join the interview call directly from my application so that I can attend the interview without leaving the platform.
ac: \* Join Call button is visible when application status is Interview Confirmed \* Clicking Join Call redirects the Independent Contractor to the meeting link in a new tab \* Button is only visible when interview has been confirmed — not before or after \* If the meeting link is unavailable, an error message is shown

title: Submit Proposal
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to submit my proposal to the Team Builder so that they can review my terms and cover letter and decide whether to send me an offer.
ac: - Submit Proposal button is available when application stage is Proposal Requested and status is Awaiting Proposal - The proposal has 3 steps: Propose Rate (trial) / Expected Salary (full-time) / Rate & Hours (part-time) → Cover Letter → Review & Send - The Team Builder sets the work, so the Independent Contractor doesn't propose tasks: on a trial role, the trial's tasks from the job post are shown read-only beside the rate and in the review, for the rate to price them; on a full-time or part-time role, the work is added once the contract starts - Trial roles ask for a monthly rate, full-time roles for an expected monthly salary, and part-time roles for a monthly rate and hours per week — the hours are pre-filled from the role and can be changed; the role summary beside the form keeps the hours it was posted at - Step 1 also asks for the day the Independent Contractor would start — today or later, opening on today for a trial and on the role's posted start otherwise; on a trial it shows the end date the trial's working days come to - The offer carries what the proposal settles — the rate or salary, the hours, the start date and the tasks — unchanged (TB-105) - Cover Letter requires a cover letter; a portfolio or work samples link is optional - Review & Send shows the whole proposal before it is sent - Independent Contractor cannot submit without completing all required fields - Submitted proposal changes status to Proposal Submitted - Team Builder is notified that a proposal has been submitted - Submit button is hidden once proposal has been submitted

title: Revise Proposal
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to revise my proposal based on the Team Builder's feedback so that I can address their concerns and move closer to an agreement.
ac: \* Revise Proposal button is available when application status is Requested Revision by TB \* Independent Contractor can view the Team Builder's revision notes before editing \* Proposal form is pre-filled with the previously submitted proposal — terms, start date and cover letter \* Independent Contractor updates the relevant fields and resubmits \* Resubmitting changes status back to Proposal Submitted \* Team Builder is notified of the resubmission - On a trial, the revision can suggest changes to the trial's tasks: change a task's name or due week, remove a task, or add a missing one, each with a required reason; the tasks stay the company's, and each suggestion is sent with the revised proposal - The Independent Contractor sees where each suggestion stands on their proposal: Accepted, Not taken, or Awaiting decision

title: View Offer
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view the full details of an offer sent to me by a Team Builder, so that I can review the terms before deciding to accept or decline.
ac: - Clicking View Offer opens the full offer details sent by the Team Builder - Shows: role, description, contract type, start date, and the tasks as the proposal settled them, each due week shown as the date it becomes - Shows the terms for the offer's type: trial — monthly rate, trial duration, and end date; full-time — monthly salary and exclusive benefits; part-time — monthly rate and hours per week - Independent Contractor can accept or decline the offer from this view - Accepting moves the engagement to active contract status

title: Accept Offer
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to accept an offer from a Team Builder so that I can formally commit to the engagement and start the contract.
ac: \* Accept Offer button is available when application stage is Offer Received and status is Awaiting Response \* Independent Contractor can review the full offer details before accepting — role, rate or salary, start date, the terms for the offer's type (trial duration, hours per week, or exclusive benefits), and the tasks the Team Builder set \* Confirmation prompt shown before accepting \* Accepting the offer changes status to Offer Accepted and card transfers to Hired stage with status Waiting to Start \* Team Builder is notified that the offer has been accepted \* Contract is created and visible in the Contracts section \* A trial offer starts a trial contract; a full-time or part-time offer starts that contract directly, with no trial and no escrow \* Accepting turns the agreed tasks into the contract's task list, where what the offer set of them — name, details, due date and priority, and who does them — stays as agreed while the agreement holds (TB-077) \* Each agreed task's due week becomes a due date counted in working weeks from the start date — on a trial, capped at its end date \* Accept button is hidden once offer has been accepted or declined - The offer carries what the proposal settled, so there's nothing to negotiate on it: the Independent Contractor accepts it or declines it (IN-075) — changes happen in the proposal, before an offer (IN-073)

title: Decline Offer
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to decline an offer (trial, full-time or part-time) so that I can remove myself from consideration if the terms are not a good fit.
ac: \* Decline button is available when application stage is Offer Received and status is Awaiting Response \* Independent Contractor can optionally provide a reason for declining \* Confirmation prompt shown before declining \* Declining changes status to Declined \* Team Builder is notified that the offer has been declined \* Card remains visible in My Applications with Declined status and a Review Offer button still accessible \* Decline button is hidden once offer has been accepted or declined

title: Message Team Builder
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to message a Team Builder directly from my application so that I can ask questions or discuss the opportunity without leaving the platform.
ac: \* Message button is available on each application card across all pipeline stages \* Clicking opens the messaging interface with that Team Builder pre-selected \* Independent Contractor can compose and send a message without leaving My Applications \* Empty message cannot be sent

title: View All Contracts
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see a list of all my active and past contracts in one place so that I can quickly overview all my ongoing and completed engagements.
ac: - All contracts listed with: company name, role, contract type (Trial/Full-Time/Part-Time), status (Active/Ended), and days remaining or end date - Default sort by most recent - Empty state shown if no contracts exist

title: Filter Contracts
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to filter my contracts by type and status so that I can focus on specific engagements.
ac: - Filter by type: Trial, Full-Time, Part-Time - Filter by status: Active, Ended - Filters can be combined - Active filters visually indicated

title: Open Contract Dashboard
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to click on a contract card to open the full contract dashboard so that I can access my tasks, performance data, and contract details for that engagement.
ac: - Clicking a Trial contract opens Trial Contract Dashboard - Clicking a Full-Time or Part-Time contract opens the Full-Time and Part-Time Contract Dashboard - Back button returns to All Contracts list

title: View Trial Dashboard
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my trial dashboard so that I can monitor my overall trial performance, tasks, activity, and fit score in one place.
ac: - Dashboard header shows: Team Builder company name, role, and contract status badges (Trial, Active) - A contract signed ahead of its start date shows Starts <date> in place of its status until that day, and the activity tracker starts counting from then rather than showing the Independent Contractor as Unresponsive - Summary stats bar shows: Tasks count, Done count, Days left with trial date range, and Waiting for review count - TFP widget shows overall score as a percentage broken down into: Performance, Profile, and Work Style — each with a progress bar and percentage - Performance is the share of trial tasks that are Done (Done trial tasks ÷ all trial tasks) - Tooltip explains how the TFP score is calculated and when the final score becomes available - Phase weights update automatically based on the current phase: On Trial (Phase 3): Work Style 20%, Profile 30%, Performance 50% — Evaluation excluded; Post Trial (Phase 4): Work Style 15%, Profile 20%, Performance 40%, Evaluation 25% - Tasks tab is the default view when the dashboard loads - Tasks tab shows the shared task list, in List view by default; what the signed offer set of its tasks shows a lock (TB-077) - The trial's tasks are the ones agreed in the signed offer, and no new tasks are added to a trial; the Independent Contractor breaks them into subtasks - The Independent Contractor moves tasks between To do and In progress and submits them for review; the Team Builder approves them or requests changes - Activity heatmap shows a GitHub-style Mon–Fri daily grid — weekends are not shown - Each tile shows one of three states: green — a task was submitted for review that day; light green — tasks were worked on (one moved or a subtask ticked); grey — no task activity that day - Current streak (consecutive weekdays with any task activity) and status label (Thriving / Idle / Unresponsive) displayed; when the trial closes, the tracker shows the final streak - Navigation tabs visible: Tasks, Contract & Payment, Evaluation - Send Message button visible in the header at all times - File a Dispute button visible in the header — available only after the trial ends - Once the trial is over the status reads Awaiting evaluation, then Evaluation received; the work is closed while it's decided (the Team Builder can still approve what's in review) and the Overview says when the evaluation is due and that the escrow is paid out with it — or on its own if it doesn't come within 5 days - The status sits beside the type badge in the header

title: Open Task Details
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to open an item in a details panel so that I can see everything about it and work on it without leaving the view I'm in.
ac: - The panel slides in over the view as the same focused sheet the Team Builder uses (TB-063) - It shows the name, status, assignee, work type, priority, start and due dates, effort, tags, what the item waits on and what it blocks, description, subtasks, and one feed of history and comments - On their own items the Independent Contractor moves the status, ticks and adds subtasks, says what the item waits on (IN-087), sends the item for review with a note, and takes a submission back - The Team Builder's planning fields read as plain text; what the signed offer set shows a lock (TB-077) - When changes were requested, the panel shows the Team Builder's note until the item is resubmitted - Notifications about an item open it in its panel

title: Switch Between Work Views
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to switch my contract's work between Board, List, Calendar, Timeline and Workload so that I can work from cards, rows, dates or a schedule.
ac: - The Work tab shows the contract's work full width — the same items the Team Builder sees; Board is the default view - The five views, search, filters, sort and grouping work as for the Team Builder (TB-131, TB-132) and are kept in the address - In Board view, the Independent Contractor drags their own cards between To do, In progress and In review — dropping on In review sends the item for review - Cards can't be dropped on Done — an item only reaches Done when the Team Builder approves it - The Team Builder's items and unassigned ones can't be moved; hovering a card says why - Due dates, effort, priority, assignee and work type are the Team Builder's to set; they are shown but not editable — the Independent Contractor sets only when their own open work starts (IN-087) - There is no Add task — the Team Builder adds the work; the Independent Contractor breaks their items into subtasks

title: Work From the Team Builder's Tasks
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want my task list to come from the Team Builder so that the work I do is the work they asked for.
ac: - The Independent Contractor doesn't add tasks — the Team Builder sets the work: a trial's tasks in its job post and the offer, which fix the trial's list, and more once the contract is a full-time or part-time role - The task list says who sets the tasks, and the Independent Contractor is notified when the Team Builder adds one: New task added - To plan a bigger task, the Independent Contractor breaks it into subtasks from the task details panel - The Independent Contractor moves tasks between To do and In progress and sends each for review when it's done - The trial's agreed tasks are what the Trial Fit Score's Performance counts

title: Move a Task Between Statuses
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to move my work between statuses so that the Team Builder can see where each piece stands.
ac: - The Independent Contractor moves their own items between To do and In progress from the panel, the status menu in the list, by dragging the card, or with Alt+Shift+Left/Right - Moving an item to In review sends it for review, with an optional note; the Team Builder is notified - While it is In review, the Independent Contractor can take it back to To do or In progress - Only the Team Builder can move an item to Done, by approving it; Done items stay Done - Each move is recorded in the item's activity feed and counts as working on tasks that day on the activity heatmap; a submission turns the day full green - A move that can't be saved goes back with the reason and a Retry

title: Submit a Task for Review
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to submit a finished task for review so that the Team Builder can approve it.
ac: - A To do or In progress task can be submitted three ways: the check circle on its row, the Send for review button in the task details panel, or dragging its card to In review in Board view - Send for review in the panel takes an optional note for the reviewer - The task moves to In review - The Team Builder is notified that a task was sent for review (e.g. 'Juan sent a task for review') - Submitting a task turns that day's activity tile green - While the task is In review, the Independent Contractor can undo the submission - The Team Builder then approves it (Done) or requests changes with a note (back to In progress)

title: View Contract & Payment Tab
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my contract terms and payment history in the Contract & Payment tab so that I can review what was agreed and track my payment activity.
ac: - Tab shows: agreed role, trial duration, start and end dates, agreed budget, and payment schedule - Payment history shows all recorded transactions for this contract with: date, transaction type, amount, and status - Transaction types: Payment Deposited, Payment Released, Payment Refunded - If a dispute has been filed for this contract, it is visible in this tab with: date filed, reason, and current status - Only 1 dispute can be filed per contract — File a Dispute button is hidden once a dispute has been submitted - Tab is read-only — no editing available from this view

title: View Evaluation
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view the evaluation submitted by my Team Builder after the trial so that I can understand their assessment of my performance and see my finalized Trial Fit Score.
ac: - Evaluation tab shows the full evaluation submitted by the Team Builder - Shows: overall star rating, written feedback, and overall recommendation - Finalized TFP score shown after evaluation - Read-only view

title: Send Message to Team Builder
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to send a message to my Team Builder directly from the trial dashboard so that I can communicate without leaving my contract view.
ac: - Send Message button is visible in the dashboard header at all times - Clicking opens the messaging interface with the Team Builder pre-selected - Independent Contractor can compose and send a message without leaving the dashboard - Empty message cannot be sent

title: View Full-Time and Part-Time Contract Overview
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my full-time or part-time contract dashboard so that I can monitor my ongoing work, tasks, and contract details in one place.
ac: - Dashboard header shows: Team Builder company name, role, and contract status badges (Full-Time or Part-Time, Active) - A contract signed ahead of its start date shows Starts <date> in place of its status until that day, and the activity tracker starts counting from then rather than showing the Independent Contractor as Unresponsive - Summary stats bar shows: Tasks count, Done count, Waiting for review count, and progress (share of tasks Done) - On a contract that converted from a trial, the Trial Fit Score widget shows the final TFP from the completed trial — read-only, does not update - On a contract hired directly with no trial, there is no trial score — the widget shows the match percentage at hire instead - Tasks tab is the default view when the dashboard loads - Tasks tab shows the shared task list — tasks are never locked, and the Team Builder can add tasks at any time while the contract is active - The Independent Contractor is notified when the Team Builder adds a task: New task added - Navigation tabs visible: Tasks, Contract & Payment, Evaluation - Send Message button visible in the header at all times - File a Dispute button visible in the header — available at any time during an active full-time or part-time contract - The status sits beside the type badge in the header - A contract that converted from a trial shows Full-time or Part-time since its start date, the next payday and amount, the benefits the signed offer included, and the trial as its first chapter (its dates, escrow, final score and evaluation) - Notice given by either side shows as Ends <date> in the header and on the Overview until the role ends; the Independent Contractor can give notice, or cancel a role before its first day, from Contract & Payment (IN-091)

title: View Task List (Full-Time / Part-Time)
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view the task list of my full-time or part-time contract so that I can see what I need to work on.
ac: - Tasks tab shows the contract's shared task list — the same list the Team Builder sees - List view is the default, grouped into collapsible sections by status (To do, In progress, In review, Done) with columns Task, Due, Priority, Added by, and Status; Board view is also available - The Team Builder can add tasks at any time while the contract is active; the first tasks from the signed offer, if it had any, stay as agreed - Rows show Overdue and Changes requested where they apply - Clicking a task opens the task details panel - An ended contract's task list is read-only

title: Break a Task into Subtasks
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to break a task into subtasks so that I can plan and track the steps of bigger pieces of work.
ac: - Subtasks are added as a checklist in the task details panel - Either side can add subtasks to a task that isn't Done - Only the Independent Contractor ticks subtasks off as they finish them - Ticked subtasks show as done to both sides - Ticking a subtask counts as working on tasks that day on the activity heatmap (light green) - Subtasks work the same on trial, full-time, and part-time contracts

title: Comment on a Task
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to comment on a task so that I can ask questions and share updates with the Team Builder right on the task.
ac: - The task details panel has a comment box under its activity feed - Either side can comment on any task, whatever its status, while the contract is live - Comments read as a comment thread, not a chat: each in its own box with the author's photo, name and time above the text, in time order with the task's history - The Team Builder is notified of each new comment, and the notification opens the task on its comments; more comments on the same task while that notification is unread update it instead of adding another - An empty comment can't be posted - An ended contract is read-only — its comments stay visible but no new ones can be added

title: Respond to Requested Changes
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see and respond to changes the Team Builder requested on a task so that I can fix the work and get it approved.
ac: - When the Team Builder requests changes, the task moves back to In progress and the Independent Contractor is notified: Changes requested on a task, with the note - The task shows the note as Changes requested until it is resubmitted - The Independent Contractor can comment on the task to ask about the changes - Resubmitting (the check circle, Send for review, or dragging the card to In review) sends the task back to In review, and the Team Builder is notified - Resubmitting clears the Changes requested note from the task; the request stays in the task's activity feed - Once a trial is over, changes can no longer be asked for, so none are left that couldn't be resubmitted

title: Undo a Submission
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to undo a task I submitted for review so that I can keep working on it if I sent it too early.
ac: - While a task is In review, the Independent Contractor can undo the submission - Undoing moves the task back to In progress - Once the Team Builder approves the task or requests changes, the submission can no longer be undone - The undo is recorded in the task's activity feed - Undo works the same on trial, full-time, and part-time contracts

title: View Contract & Payment Tab
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my full-time or part-time contract terms, pay, exclusive benefits, and payment history so that I can keep track of my compensation and financial activity.
ac: - Full-time: tab shows agreed role, contract start date, base salary, exclusive benefits breakdown, and payment schedule - Exclusive benefits listed separately: Health Insurance, Government Contribution, Internet Allowance, Learning & Development Allowance - Part-time: tab shows agreed role, contract start date, monthly rate, hours per week, and payment schedule — part-time contracts have no exclusive benefits - Payment history shows all recorded transactions with: date, transaction type, amount, and status - If a dispute has been filed for this contract, it is visible in this tab with: date filed, reason, and current status - One dispute can be filed per chapter of the contract (the trial, then the role it became) — File a Dispute is hidden once one has been submitted for the current chapter - Tab is read-only

title: View Evaluation Tab
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view all evaluations submitted by my Team Builder in the Evaluation tab so that I can track ongoing feedback and understand how I am being assessed.
ac: - Evaluation tab shows all evaluations submitted by the Team Builder during the full-time or part-time engagement - Each entry shows: date submitted, star rating, and written feedback - Read-only view

title: View Trial Fit Score
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my Trial Fit Score from my full-time or part-time contract dashboard so that I can reference the score that led to my hire.
ac: - TFP widget visible on the Full-Time and Part-Time Contract Dashboard for reference - On a contract that converted from a trial, it shows the final score from the completed trial - Read-only — the score does not change after the full-time or part-time contract begins - On a contract hired directly with no trial, there is no trial score — the widget shows the match percentage at hire instead - On a trial it is final as soon as the trial's evaluation is sent — not only once a full-time or part-time role begins

title: Respond to a Post-Trial Hire Offer
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to review and respond to the full-time or part-time offer a Team Builder sends after my trial so that I can decide whether to keep working with them.
ac: - The Independent Contractor is notified when the Team Builder sends a full-time or part-time offer after the trial, and the offer can be opened from the trial contract - Offer shows: role, contract type (Full-Time or Part-Time), start date, pay (monthly salary for full-time; monthly rate and hours per week for part-time), monthly payment schedule, and the services agreement - A full-time offer also lists which exclusive benefits are included; a part-time offer has none - To accept, the Independent Contractor signs by typing their full name and agreeing to the platform terms - Accepting releases any escrow still held for the trial to the Independent Contractor, and the contract continues as full-time or part-time - After accepting, the Trial Fit Score is frozen at its final trial value - Team Builder is notified when the offer is accepted - Decline is available with an optional reason; the Team Builder is notified, with the reason if one was given - Declining leaves the trial contract and its record as they are - If the Team Builder withdraws the offer, it shows as withdrawn and can no longer be accepted - Once answered, the offer is read-only and shows Accepted, Declined, or Withdrawn - An offer still out when the Team Builder ends the contract is withdrawn, and can't be accepted - The offer says to answer by its start date; one not answered by then expires — it can no longer be accepted or declined, it shows as Expired, and the Independent Contractor is told the company can send a new one - Accepting is refused with the reason (expired, withdrawn, or the contract ended) rather than appearing to succeed

title: View Team Builder Company Profile
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view the Team Builder's company profile from my full-time or part-time contract dashboard so that I can stay informed about the company I work for.
ac: - Company profile shows: company logo, company name, description, industry, location, company URL, and work style badges - Read-only view from the contract dashboard

title: Send Message to Team Builder
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to send a message to my Team Builder directly from the full-time or part-time contract dashboard so that I can communicate without leaving my contract view.
ac: - Send Message button visible in the dashboard header at all times - Clicking opens the messaging interface with the Team Builder pre-selected - Empty message cannot be sent

title: Receive Payment
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to receive confirmation when my pay (a full-time salary or a part-time monthly rate) is recorded on schedule so that I know my earnings have been processed.
ac: - Independent Contractor receives in-app and email notification when their pay is recorded - Notification includes: contract name, amount, and payment schedule period - Payment appears in Earnings → Transaction History immediately - Amount matches the agreed pay from the contract (a full-time salary or a part-time monthly rate) - On a full-time or part-time contract each month is paid on its last day — pro rata for a month it started or ended in — and Contract & Payment shows the next payday and amount - While a dispute about the role is open, its amount is kept back from the payday and the payment says so; it is paid out, or refunded, when the case closes - Under notice, the last payday is the notice's last day, pro rata; ended today by the company, the pay runs through the notice's last day and says it is in lieu of notice

title: File a Dispute
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to file a dispute at any point during my full-time or part-time engagement so that I can raise concerns about payment or the engagement.
ac: - File a Dispute button is available at any time during an active full-time or part-time contract — not before its first day (it says the day filing opens) and not once the contract has ended (it says it can't be disputed any more); the same rule is checked again when the dispute is saved - Only 1 dispute can be filed per contract — the button is hidden after one has been submitted; while one is open from either side it opens that case instead - Dispute form requires: reason, description and amount in question; screenshots and PDFs (up to 6, 10 MB each) and a link are optional - Allowed reason codes: Missing Deliverable, Out-of-Scope Output, Missed Deadline, No Report Submitted - The dispute can't be submitted until every required field is complete - Filing opens it as a case: the Team Builder is notified and has 5 days to respond — if they don't, it closes in the Independent Contractor's favor - Filed dispute appears in the Contract & Payment tab of this contract and in Earnings → Sent Disputes as Pending; the filer goes straight to its case page - On a contract that converted from a trial, filing stays available once the trial's escrow is paid out: the dispute is about the pay, up to a month's pay - On a full-time or part-time role there is no escrow, so the amount in question (up to a month's pay) is kept back from the next payday while the case is open, and the Independent Contractor is told their pay is held. When it closes, what was kept back is paid on, refunded to the company, or split as agreed; a refund bigger than what was kept back comes off the following pay - One dispute per chapter: the trial and the full-time or part-time role it became each get their own, so a dispute filed (or withdrawn) about the trial doesn't stop one about the role; only one case can be open at a time - A refusal says why: a case already open, the timing, or the amount

title: View Earnings Overview
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see a summary of my total earnings across all contracts so that I can quickly understand my overall payment activity on the platform.
ac: - Earnings page shows a summary card with: total amount received across all contracts - Summary is updated in real time as new transactions are recorded

title: View Transaction History
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see a full list of all payment transactions across all my contracts so that I can track my complete earnings history in one place.
ac: - Transaction History shows all recorded payment activity across all contracts - Each row shows: date, contract name, Team Builder company name, transaction type, amount, and status - Transaction types: Payment Received, Payment Refunded - Default sort by most recent - Pagination applied - Empty state shown if no transactions exist

title: Filter Transactions
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to filter my transactions by contract, status, and date range so that I can narrow down records to find what I am looking for.
ac: - Filter options: by contract name, by status (Received, Refunded), by date range - Filters can be combined - Active filters are visually indicated - Clearing filters restores the full list

title: Search Transactions
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to search my transactions so that I can quickly locate a specific payment record.
ac: - Search bar available on Earnings page - Searches by contract name or Team Builder company name - Results update dynamically as Independent Contractor types - Empty state shown when no results match

title: View Transaction Detail
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to open a specific transaction to view its full details so that I can verify the payment amount, source, and date.
ac: - Clicking a transaction opens the detail view - Shows: date, contract name, Team Builder company name, transaction type, amount, and status - Read-only view

title: View Sent Disputes
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see all disputes I have filed across all contracts in one list so that I can monitor the status of each dispute.
ac: - Sent Disputes lists every dispute the Independent Contractor has filed across all contracts; Received lists the ones filed against them - Each row shows: date filed, contract name and reason, the other party, amount, who the case is waiting on (with the time left on their turn), and status (Pending / Resolved / Rejected / Withdrawn) - Rows waiting on this person say so and open with Respond; every row opens the case page - Default sort by most recent; search and a status filter narrow the list - Empty state shown if no disputes have been filed

title: View Dispute Detail
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to open a specific dispute to view its full details and status updates so that I can stay informed on the process check outcome.
ac: - Each dispute opens as a case page, from the list, the contract or any notification about it - A banner says whose turn it is and until when ("It's your turn to respond — by Tue 30 Sep, 9:00 AM (5 days left)"), what happens if the time runs out, or how the case ended - A strip shows where each side stands — the company, the independent and Hireable support — with the one whose turn it is highlighted - One timeline shows everything in order, each entry marked with who it's from: the filing (reason, amount, description, files), each side's responses and additions, support's questions and deadline changes, settlement proposals and answers, and the outcome - Screenshots open full size and PDFs open in a new tab; both sides and support see the same files - The side panel shows the amount in question and where it stands, the contract's payments — escrow funded, paid to the independent, refunded to the company, still pending in escrow — and the contract, with a link to it - The Team Builder and Hireable support read the same case; nothing on it can be edited after it's sent

title: Withdraw Dispute
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to withdraw a pending dispute so that I can cancel it if the issue has been resolved or I have changed my mind.
ac: - Withdraw dispute is in the case page's header, for the party who filed it, while the case is open - Confirmation prompt shown before withdrawing - Dispute status changes to Withdrawn and an open settlement proposal is closed with it - Hireable admin sees the withdrawal as new activity and the Team Builder is notified that the dispute has been withdrawn - Once withdrawn, a new dispute cannot be filed for the same contract

title: View Profile
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my full profile so that I can see exactly how I appear to Team Builders.
ac: - Profile shows: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, website, LinkedIn, bio, workplace tags, skills, and performance history - Displays exactly how the profile appears to Team Builders - Edit and Retake Quiz buttons available

title: Edit Profile
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to edit my profile details such as photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, website, and LinkedIn so that I can keep my professional information accurate and up to date.
ac: - Edit Profile form allows updating: photo, name, role, rate, experience level, location, website, LinkedIn - All changes saved immediately - Validation applied to required fields - Updated profile reflects immediately on Team Builder-facing view

title: Edit Bio
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to write and update my bio so that I can describe my background and value proposition to potential Team Builders.
ac: - Bio section shows current bio text - Edit Bio opens a text editor - Character limit applies (500 characters) - Changes saved immediately

title: View Workplace Tags
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my workplace tags derived from my work style quiz so that I can see the personality and work style badges that Team Builders see on my profile.
ac: - Workplace Tags section shows current tags derived from work style quiz - Tags are display-only and cannot be manually edited - Retake Quiz button available to update them

title: Retake Work Style Quiz
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to retake the work style quiz from my profile so that I can update my workplace tags if my working style or preferences have changed.
ac: - Retake Quiz button available on Profile page - Independent Contractor prompted to confirm before restarting - Completing quiz updates workplace tags/badges - New badges replace old ones immediately - Match % recalculates based on new work style results

title: Edit Skills
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to add or remove skills on my profile so that my skill set accurately reflects my current capabilities.
ac: - Edit Skills section shows current skills as tags - Independent Contractor can add new skills by typing and selecting from suggestions - Independent Contractor can remove skills by clicking the remove icon - Changes saved immediately - Updated skills reflect on Team Builder-facing profile

title: View Performance History
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view my performance history showing past evaluations, star ratings, and Team Builder feedback per contract so that I can track my professional growth.
ac: - Performance History section shows all past evaluations received - Each entry shows: company name, role, contract type (Trial / Full-Time / Part-Time), date, star rating, and written feedback - Visible to Team Builders viewing the profile - Read-only — Independent Contractor cannot edit or remove entries

title: View / Edit Account
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to view and edit my account information so that I can keep my basic account details current.
ac: - Account page shows: name, email, account type (Independent Contractor) - Independent Contractor can edit name and email - Email change requires re-verification - Changes saved immediately

title: Change Password
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to change my account password from the Security settings so that I can keep my account secure.
ac: - Form requires: current password, new password, confirm new password - New password must meet minimum requirements (8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 number) - Incorrect current password shows an error - Success message shown after change

title: Add / Manage Payment Method
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to add or manage my payment method so that I have a verified destination for receiving payments from the platform.
ac: - Payment Method page shows all saved payment methods - Independent Contractor can add new method, set default, or remove existing - Removal confirmation prompt shown - At least one payment method must remain active

title: Work Views, Search and Filters
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want the same views, search, filters, sort and grouping as the Team Builder so that I can find and plan my work my way.
ac: - The Work tab offers Board, List, Calendar, Timeline and Workload, all over the contract's one list (TB-131) - Search, filters, sort and grouping work as for the Team Builder and are kept in the address (TB-132) - The Overview tab is the Team Builder's (TB-143) from the Independent Contractor's side: a banner and Needs attention for work sent back with changes and their own overdue items, then progress, what's due next and recent changes, beside the Trial Fit Score or Match at hire, the activity log and the company, whose profile opens from there - Message and File a dispute stay in the header row on every tab - Changes are saved or clearly refused, the same way (TB-144)

title: Break Work Down and Discuss It
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to break my work into subtasks and comment on it so that I can plan my steps and keep the Team Builder in the loop.
ac: - On their own To do and In progress items the Independent Contractor adds, ticks and removes subtasks — Add subtask opens a new row with the cursor in it that works like adding a task: Enter adds the subtask and leaves the row open for the next, Enter on nothing or Escape closes it (and only it, not the panel), and clicking elsewhere keeps what was typed; progress shows as done of total — an item without subtasks shows no percentage - Both sides comment on any item while the contract runs; comments and the item's history read as one feed - Subtask ticks count as working on tasks that day on the activity heatmap

title: See the Plan
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to see the dates, effort, dependencies and workload the Team Builder has set so that I know what's expected and when.
ac: - Start and due dates, effort, work type, priority, tags and dependencies are visible on cards, rows, the panel, the calendar and the timeline - Due dates, effort, work type, priority and tags are the Team Builder's to set: the Independent Contractor sees them as plain text, and a change made any other way is refused — except what a signed offer set of a task (its name, description, due date, priority and assignee), which shows a lock to both sides (TB-077) - The start date is theirs too on their own To do and In progress items: from the panel, or by dragging the bar's left end on the timeline; starting the work sets it to that day if it wasn't earlier (TB-136) - So are dependencies: on their own items that aren't Done, the Independent Contractor adds and removes what the item waits on, with the same checks against loops (TB-139); on anyone else's item they only read them - Blocked work is marked in words, with what it waits on in the panel - The Workload view shows the Independent Contractor's load next to the Team Builder's, in relative effort — not hours, with no capacity line

title: Respond to a Dispute
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to answer a dispute on my turn, with the screenshots that back me up, so that the case is decided on both sides of the story.
ac: - When a dispute is filed against the Independent Contractor, or Hireable support asks them a question, it's their turn: they have 5 days to respond - A response carries text (required), screenshots and PDFs (up to 6, 10 MB each) and an optional link; sending it hands the case to Hireable support for review - A reminder is sent when one day is left; if the time runs out with no response, the case closes in the Team Builder's favor and the money moves as a ruling would - When it isn't their turn they can still add information for support, with files; it doesn't change whose turn it is - the Team Builder is notified of every response and addition, and can read it on the case

title: Settle a Dispute
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to settle a dispute with the Team Builder by splitting the amount in question so that I'm paid what we agree without waiting for a ruling.
ac: - Either side can propose a settlement while the case is open: how the amount in question splits between a refund to the company and a release to the independent - Quick splits (all to one side, half each) and two amounts that fill each other in; the two parts must add up to the amount in question - The Team Builder is notified and sees the proposal on the case with Accept and Decline; a newer proposal from either side replaces the open one - Accepting — confirmed first — closes the case as Resolved by agreement and moves both parts straight away, never more than the escrow still holds - Declining keeps the case going and tells the proposer

title: End a Full-Time or Part-Time Contract
story: As an Independent Contractor, I want to end a contract myself — with the notice my agreement gives, or before it has started — so that I am not tied to a role only the company can close.
ac: - Before the contract's first day (a signed trial, or a full-time or part-time role not started yet), the Independent Contractor can cancel it from the Contract & Payment tab: nothing is owed, a trial's escrow goes back to the company, and the Team Builder is notified - On a running full-time or part-time role, Give notice ends it after 30 days (full-time) or 14 days (part-time), as the services agreement says; a confirmation shows the last day first - Until the notice's last day the role carries on as normal: the work stays open, pay is recorded at the end of each month, and the last pay is pro rata to the last day - The Team Builder is notified when notice is given; both sides see Ends <date> in the header and a notice callout on the Overview - The Independent Contractor can take back notice they gave before its last day, and the Team Builder is told; notice the company gave shows here too, read-only - The Independent Contractor can't end a running role at once — that is notice, as the agreement says — and can't end the trial after it: the company decides what's next - When notice runs out, the contract ends on its own and both sides are told, with the last pay recorded

title: View Admin Dashboard Overview

ac: - Dashboard loads upon admin login showing platform-wide health metrics - Displays key stat widgets: total users, active contracts, open disputes, revenue - All widgets are clickable and navigate to relevant modules - Data refreshes in real time or on page load

title: View Platform Stats
story: As an admin, I want to view key platform statistics including total users, active contracts, roles, and revenue so that I can monitor platform performance at a glance.
ac: - Platform Stats page shows: total registered users (broken down by Team Builder and Independent Contractor), total active contracts, total roles, total disputes, and total platform revenue - Stats are shown with period comparison (e.g. vs last month) - Visual charts/graphs used where appropriate

title: View All Team Builders
story: As an admin, I want to see a table of all Team Builder accounts on the platform showing name, email, status, and date joined so that I can manage and monitor all Team Builder accounts in one place.
ac: - Team Builders table shows: name, email, company, status, date joined, and total roles - Default sort by most recent - Pagination applied - Empty state shown if no Team Builders exist

title: Search Team Builders
story: As an admin, I want to search Team Builders by name or email so that I can quickly locate a specific Team Builder account.
ac: - Search by name or email - Results update dynamically as admin types - Empty state shown when no results match

title: Filter Team Builders by Status
story: As an admin, I want to filter Team Builders by status (Active, Suspended, Inactive, Pending Verification) so that I can focus on specific groups that need attention.

title: View / Update Team Builder Status
